oneLiner.en: Opening the sixth perek of Pirkei Avos, the Mashgiach explains that the chachamim who learn Torah lishmah become one with the Torah, so that even their names and their ordinary words carry holiness.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach begins with the sixth perek of Avos, a baraisa added to the five perakim and learned before Shavuos, a time when a Jew can always begin anew. He asks why the baraisa names the chachamim when there is no dispute, and answers that one who learns Torah lishmah unites with the Torah, like meat in a fire that becomes fire, so his very name is Torah. Mentioning a holy name draws down kedushah, as with Chevron in the Beis Hamikdash and Eretz Yisrael in Moshe's words. The word 'mishnah' suggests doubling: tzaddikim speak to people while addressing Hashem, as David did with Naval, illustrated by stories of tzaddikim. Turning to Torah lishmah, he explains that the same Torah is received through each person's middah, discusses lishmah and shelo lishmah, and ends with how refined things, like wine for Kiddush and Olam Haba, are the most easily affected.

en: The sixth perek of Avos is a baraisa added to the five perakim in the style of the Mishnah, and it is learned at the time of Shavuos.
The Mashgiach says a Jew must always be able to lift himself up and begin a new account, without being held back by his past.
The names of the chachamim are themselves Torah, because one who learns lishmah becomes united with the Torah.
Mentioning a holy name, of a tzaddik, of Chevron or of Eretz Yisrael, draws down kedushah and salvation.
Tzaddikim can say one thing with several meanings, speaking to people while really addressing the Ribono shel Olam.
Each person receives the same Torah according to his own middah and level, and learns lishmah as far as his level allows.
The more refined a thing is, the more easily it is affected, as with wine for Kiddush and with Olam Haba.

candidateTopics: receiving Torah according to one's middah

title.en: The sixth perek and renewal before Shavuos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the sixth perek is a baraisa added to Avos in the language of the Mishnah. He speaks of the time before Shavuos as one when a Jew can always begin anew, and notes that the parsha of Mattan Torah follows the parsha of Yisro.

title.en: Why the chachamim are named

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the baraisa gives the names of the chachamim when there is no dispute. He answers that one who learns Torah lishmah becomes united with the Torah, like meat in a fire that becomes fire, so his name itself is Torah and mentioning it draws down blessing.

title.en: Chevron and Eretz Yisrael: the power of mentioning

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that in the Beis Hamikdash they announced the dawn by mentioning Chevron, to recall the Avos buried there, and asks why Moshe Rabbeinu mentions Eretz Yisrael so often. Merely mentioning a holy place or name, he explains, draws down kedushah.

title.en: The shoemaker who said the Rebbe's name

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a simple chassid, a shoemaker, who constantly repeated his Rebbe's name with a wish for his health as he worked. He then speaks of the words of Torah as burning fire.

title.en: Mishnah as doubling: David's words to Naval

summary.en: On 'baruch shebachar bahem uvemishnasam', the Mashgiach explains that 'mishnah' suggests doubling: tzaddikim say one thing with several meanings. He asks how David HaMelech could greet the wicked Naval with blessings, and answers that he was really speaking to the Ribono shel Olam, so it was not flattery.

title.en: Reb Naftali of Ropshitz and worldly talk

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells a story of Reb Naftali of Ropshitz involving a request about milk. He returns to 'shanu chachamim bilshon hamishnah': the chachamim could speak with people about ordinary things while their words were about far higher matters.

title.en: Torah lishmah and a story of a salvation

summary.en: The Mashgiach begins the first mishnah, 'kol ha'osek baTorah lishmah', and speaks of each person learning according to his own path. He then tells a story of a sick man whom the doctors could not help, a messenger sent to a Rebbe, and a salvation that came at that very time.

title.en: One Torah through different middos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that each person receives the Torah according to his root and middah, as the Torah of Beis Shammai came through their middah. He compares it to water poured into glasses of different colors: the water looks different, yet it is the same water and the same Torah.

title.en: Lishmah, shelo lishmah and the rewards

summary.en: The Mashgiach discusses Torah lishmah and shelo lishmah: each person learns according to his level, and from shelo lishmah one comes to lishmah, yet this is no reason to become lax. He goes through the rewards the mishnah lists for one who learns lishmah.

title.en: Refined things: wine, Kiddush and Olam Haba

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the more refined a thing is, the more easily it is affected: wine becomes forbidden through a goy's touch, and some are careful even about his look, because wine is used for Kiddush and is likened to Olam Haba. He concludes that Olam Haba is so delicate that even a glance can affect it, and returns to learning lishmah.

catalogTitle: פרקי אבות: פרק קנין תורה: גדלות הצדיקים' ביאור ענין תורה לשמה וגודל גן עדן של לומד תורה לשמה

oneLiner.en: On the opening Mishnah of Avos, the Mashgiach traces the chain of the Torah from Moshe at Sinai to the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah and on to our own weak generation of 'broken luchos', explaining what each link teaches and how the Torah is held today.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Avos 1:1 and explains why the Oral Torah could not be written: it is inscribed on the heart and mouth of the Jew, a private code of Hashem and His people. With the Bartenura he explains why Avos begins at Sinai, and reads 'from Sinai' as the lesson of humility of the lowest mountain, which made Moshe, and after him Yehoshua, the vessel for the Torah. He then follows the chain to the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, who restored the praise 'the great, mighty and awesome' because they spoke for the Jewish people, the kallah, while the prophets spoke for Hashem. He describes our era after the recent churban as a time of silence and of 'broken luchos', with hidden leaders whom one finds by following the old footsteps, and ends with the three directives of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah as the answer to the weakening of the generations.

en: The Oral Torah is written on the heart and mouth of the Jew who learns properly, so it cannot be put in writing or truly reached by the nations.
'Moshe received the Torah from Sinai' means through the humility of Sinai, the lowest mountain; Yehoshua merited to succeed Moshe for the same humility and devotion.

The Anshei Knesses HaGedolah spoke for Knesses Yisroel and opened the era of the Oral Torah, which flows from Jewish hearts; therefore they could restore praises of Hashem that the prophets had left out.
Our era is one of silence and of 'broken luchos': the task is to preserve what was received, not to create new things, and to hold on to the thread of the mesorah.
The three directives of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah answer three ways the generations weaken: in Torah knowledge, in the number of learners, and in yiras Shamayim.

candidateTopics: Oral Torah and the Jewish heart
humility as the vessel for Torah
broken luchos and the last generations

title.en: Why the Oral Torah cannot be written

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with 'Moshe received the Torah from Sinai' and brings that Moshe wanted the Oral Torah written, but the nations would then claim to be Israel. He explains that the Oral Torah is written on the heart and mouth of the Jew, a secret code only a Jewish heart understands, so even in translation it is not theirs.

title.en: Received 'from Sinai': the lesson of humility

summary.en: With the Bartenura the Mashgiach explains why Avos, which deals with middos, opens with Sinai. He reads 'from Sinai' as 'because of Sinai': Hashem chose the lowest mountain, and Moshe reasoned that as the humblest man he must receive the Torah. The name Chorev teaches that one who lives a life of luxury cannot be a vessel for Torah.

title.en: Why Yehoshua received the Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Yehoshua was not Moshe's greatest student, yet he merited to succeed him through humility, as Moshe saw when he renamed him. He links this to the days of Sefirah as days of humility before Kabbalas HaTorah, and describes how Yehoshua served Moshe and prepared the beis medrash, like the moon that has no light of its own.

title.en: Restoring 'the great, mighty and awesome'

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the eras of the Zekeinim, the Neviim and the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, who 'restored the crown': prophets had dropped 'mighty' and 'awesome' when they saw the churban, and the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah put them back, since a lamb surviving among seventy wolves is itself Hashem's might. He adds that praise of Hashem must fit the time and the situation.

title.en: The Anshei Knesses HaGedolah speak for the kallah

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why they are called the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah and explains that with them the written Torah ended and the era of the Oral Torah began, Torah that flows from Jewish hearts. The prophets speak for Hashem, the chassan; the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah speak for Knesses Yisroel, the kallah, as in the Berditchever's reading of Pesach and Chag HaMatzos. So in galus they could proclaim the praise that the prophets had left out.

title.en: From 'received' to an era of silence

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the Mishnah says Moshe 'received' and not that Hashem 'gave over' the Torah: no human can take over the infinite Torah, but Moshe gave over all of it to Yehoshua. He continues the chain through Tannaim, Amoraim, Geonim, Rishonim and Acharonim, and calls our time a new era of poverty and silence after a churban greater than earlier ones, a time to preserve rather than create.

title.en: The generation of broken luchos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the last words of the Torah allude to the broken luchos, and these are the last generations before Moshiach. Yet broken luchos also lie in the aron, and the chain from teacher to student cannot stop; hidden, small leaders are found by following, as Shir HaShirim says, the footsteps of the flock, those who keep the old ways, and not those who invent new ones.

title.en: Leaders chosen by people, and our deafness

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that today's leaders are not luchos from heaven but are appointed by people, and gives the sign for the true ones: 'the words that were on the first luchos', no new paths. He recalls that in the Chofetz Chaim's time all of Klal Yisroel knew who its leaders were, and says that today the weakness is ours: we have become deaf and do not hear.

title.en: Holding the thread: today's might of Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares the mesorah to pearls on a thread: today no pearls are seen, only the thread, and holding it is the lifeline. A Jew who still davens and learns while the wolves of the yetzer hara tear at his words is the 'might and awe' of Hashem today. He suggests that the number 120 of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah reflects the twelve tribes, all of Klal Yisroel.

title.en: Three directives for weakening generations

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that from the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah on, each generation only 'receives' and grows weaker, so they gave three directives. Be deliberate in judgment, because the special siyata diShmaya of earlier poskim, seen in stories of the Chasam Sofer and Rabbi Akiva Eiger, is gone; raise many students because fewer learn; and make a fence because yiras Shamayim has weakened.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: לראות הבורא בבריאתו' שלא לפרוק עול' להיות תמים' ולעבוד הקב"ה לשם שמים (שייכות לפרשת שלח)

oneLiner.en: Speaking to bochurim before they leave for the country in the summer, the Mashgiach teaches that every person is Hashem's shliach and must not forget whose mission he is on: to see the Creator in His creation, to serve Him with temimus and truth away from politics, and to make Hashem beloved through fine middos.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Chasam Sofer on why the meraglim failed although Moshe Rabbeinu sent them: according to Devarim the people asked for the mission, so the spies were the people's agents. Every person, he continues, is sent down by Hashem on a mission, and summer travel, which begins in the season of the meraglim, is a chance to repair their journey. Through the Ba'al Shem Tov, a story of Reb Shimon of Yaroslav and the angel's answer to Yaakov, he shows that the yetzer hara's task is to make a person forget his mission. In the country one should see Hashem's greatness in the stars and in nature. A second point is temimus and emes in the generation before Moshiach: avoiding politics and disputes, loving every Jew, davening warmly, and making Hashem beloved, with the story of a son-in-law who learned ten years for a cat.

en: Every person is a shliach whom Hashem sent down from Heaven to gather pearls of Torah and mitzvos in this world.
Hashem directs every journey, and a person often does not know the real purpose of his trip; bochurim going to the country must remember whose shliach they are.
In the country one can see the greatness of the Creator in the stars, in a stream and in a tree, and this contemplation is part of the mission.
A Jew must serve Hashem with temimus and emes, without politics, cleverness or involvement in disputes between groups.
One must make Hashem beloved to others through refined middos and warm davening, not through coarseness or provocation.

candidateTopics: emes in the generation before Moshiach

title.en: Why the meraglim failed

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the meraglim failed if a shliach carries the power of the one who sent him and Moshe Rabbeinu sent them. He brings the Chasam Sofer: in Devarim the people asked for the mission, so the spies were really the people's agents, unlike Yehoshua's spies in the haftarah, who succeeded.

title.en: Every person is Hashem's shliach

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares the soul sent down to this world to a diver gathering pearls from the sea bottom. Summer travel begins in the season of the meraglim's journey, and with the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'mei'Hashem mitzadei gever' he explains that Hashem sends a person to a place, like a man sent to Chicago to make a brachah on water that holds a spark he must repair.

title.en: The brandy without a brachah; whose shliach am I

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how Reb Shimon of Yaroslav told a customer that his father's soul was in the brandy he drank without a brachah on the yahrzeit. He applies it to the summer months: travel is a tikkun for the meraglim, and a person must ask whether he is Hashem's shliach or the yetzer hara's.

title.en: The angel's answer to Yaakov

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Yaakov's question to the angel, who is the yetzer hara, and Rashi that an angel's name is his mission. He pictures stopping people on 13th Avenue to ask what their mission is, and explains that the angel's 'why do you ask my name' is itself his mission: to make people never ask what their mission is.

title.en: Seeing the Creator in the country

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the country's opportunities: saying Tehillim by a stream, watching a sunrise, and looking at the stars as Yeshaya says. He describes the speed of light and stars whose light takes thousands of years to arrive, and how small a person feels, yet Hashem lowers Himself to watch over every creature. With the Maggid of Mezritch on 'melo ha'aretz kinyanecha' he says the whole world is full of ways to know Hashem.

title.en: Hakol yoducha and the false freedom of the country

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that on Shabbos one praises the Creation in 'Hakol yoducha', and tells how Reb Eizikel of Ziditchov's 'Hakol yoducha' in Sighet brought listeners to tears. He then attacks the common lie that the country is a time to be free of all restraint, mentions a bochur who took off his tzitzis to play ball, and notes that the parsha of the meraglim ends with tzitzis, the reminder of whose shliach one is.

title.en: Temimus and emes in the generation of the heels

summary.en: As a second point, the Mashgiach teaches that a bochur must go with temimus, without tricks. He describes the generations as one body, from the dor hamidbar as the head to our generation as the heels, jokes about a 'convention of heels', and explains that the last word of Shema, emes, does not appear in the Torah's text because truth is missing before Moshiach, as the Gemara at the end of Sotah says.

title.en: The meraglim's politics

summary.en: The Mashgiach links temimus to Yaakov, the man of truth, and warns against the politics that fill even the frum world. The whole sin of the meraglim was politics: as nesiim they feared new leaders in Eretz Yisroel, and he brings the Chiddushei HaRim on Korach that the generation before Moshiach faces the same test. He tells the bochurim not to get involved in disputes between groups and to hold on to truth even when it is hidden.

title.en: Loving every Jew, warm davening, making Hashem beloved

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks the bochurim to love and respect Jews of every group and never speak or think disparagingly of them, and to daven warmly but not wildly, which sanctifies Hashem's Name. He explains 'yoshvei kranos' as people in the beis medrash who sit with horns, warns against provoking others in the name of chassidus, and explains 've'ahavta' as making Hashem beloved through refined middos.

title.en: Ten years of learning for a cat; parting words

summary.en: The Mashgiach retells a story from Rabbi Feivel Mendlowitz about a son-in-law on kest who learned every night for ten years because he thought the noise in the attic was his father-in-law, and found at the end it was a family of cats; everything must be for Hashem. He closes by saying the country is for gathering strength and drawing close to Hashem, and wishes the bochurim success and that they meet again in joy.

title.en: L'chaim and niggun

summary.en: L'chaim, talk and singing.

catalogTitle: פרה אדומה - A מצוה that is Above our Understanding

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parah Adumah, the chok no one can understand, is the cure for the sin of Adam HaRishon, who wanted to understand beyond his reach, and that its lesson of faith and waiting prepares the Jewish people for Nisan and the Geulah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the halachos of Parah Adumah: since we have no red heifer, all are tamei, yet hearing Parshas Parah removes the inner tumah. He links Parah to Purim: Purim comforts those left outside the camp, while Parah purifies them and brings them in, preparing for Parshas HaChodesh and Nisan. On Rosh Chodesh Nisan the Satan argues that the Jews are unworthy of redemption; Parah, a chok done without reason, answers that Hashem may redeem without reason. He traces tumah to the Nachash, who is the Satan, and to Adam and Chava's desire for intellect beyond their reach, which brought death, the highest tumah, into the world. Doing a mitzvah without understanding is the tikkun. Two things are closed to the mind: how Parah works and when Moshiach will come. Judaism is built on waiting, since the first sin, the golden calf and Shaul's failure were all failures to wait, while Dovid waited.

en: Without a red heifer everyone today is tamei from contact with the dead, but hearing Parshas Parah removes the inner tumah that blocks a person from kedushah.
Parshas Parah completes Purim: Purim comforts those outside the camp, while Parah purifies them and lets them enter.
Parah, a chok kept without understanding, answers the Satan's claim on Rosh Chodesh Nisan that the Jews have no reason to be redeemed.
Death, brought by the sin of the Eitz HaDaas, is itself tumah, and Parah Adumah is the antidote to the venom of the Nachash.
The sin of Adam was wanting to understand beyond his reach, and doing a mitzvah without understanding is its tikkun.
Judaism is built on waiting, because the first sin was a failure to wait.

candidateTopics: Rosh Chodesh Nisan and the Geulah

title.en: Tumah today and the reading of Parah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the red heifer and explains that without it everyone today is tamei and cannot go up on Har HaBayis. He says that hearing Parshas Parah with faith removes the inner tumah, as a body has a neshamah, so tumah has an outer and an inner part.

title.en: Parah as the completion of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach ties Parah to Pur through the gematria and brings that Parshas Parah continues Purim, since Shabbos lifts up the week. Purim saves those expelled from the camp but leaves them outside; Parah purifies them and brings them in, so they enter Parshas HaChodesh renewed.

title.en: Nisan and the Satan's accusation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Nisan is the month of birth and redemption, and that on Rosh Chodesh Nisan kings are appointed in Heaven. The good malachim move that Hashem become King and Moshiach come, but the Satan argues the Jews are not worthy and the matter is put off.

title.en: A chok beyond understanding answers the Satan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parah is a chok that even Shlomo HaMelech could not understand, and that keeping it shows Klal Yisrael's deep emunah. Since Jews do a mitzvah without a reason, Hashem can redeem them without a reason. Parshas Parah is the deepest Shabbos of the year, the last one feeding the week of Adar.

title.en: The Nachash, the Satan and the lure of intellect

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks where the yetzer hara comes from and explains that Adam and Chava had no inner desires before the sin. The Nachash and the Satan are one, as their gematria shows; he could only tempt them with higher understanding, the knowledge of good and bad.

title.en: Death is tumah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that death, the punishment for the sin, is really tumah, which is why a corpse is the highest level of tumah. Life is the G-dliness in a person; the malach hamaves pulls it out and injects tumah, and Parah Adumah is the antidote to that venom.

title.en: A mitzvah without understanding as the tikkun

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that tumas meis came because Adam and Chava wanted understanding beyond them, so its cure is a mitzvah done without understanding. Understanding is a fringe benefit, not a condition for keeping mitzvos; Parah brings life, as its mayim chaim and the passuk about the tzaddik living by his emunah show.

title.en: Two closed doors: Parah and the time of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach says we are in ikvesa d'meshicha and names two things the mind may not enter: how Parah works and when Moshiach will come. He brings Yaakov Avinu, Daniel and Achashverosh's miscalculation, and compares the Jews' disappointment then to the disappointment after the Holocaust.

title.en: Judaism is built on waiting

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a Jew must wait, and contrasts a gentile served breakfast in bed with a Jew who must wash, daven and make hamotzi before eating. He brings the Ohr HaChaim that the Eitz HaDaas was a vine whose grapes Adam was meant to keep for Kiddush on Shabbos, so the first sin was not waiting.

title.en: The egel, Shaul and Dovid: waiting for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that at Matan Torah death could have ended, but the golden calf came from not waiting for Moshe Rabbeinu. Shaul lost his kingdom for not waiting for Shmuel, while Dovid waited for the sound in the treetops, so Moshiach comes from him. He ends that waiting for Moshiach is waiting for the world to be sprinkled with Parah.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: יש לנו שליחות ותכלית בכל מקום' ימים קשים אבל יכולים להגיע בהם למדרגות גבוהות (שייכות לפרשת בהעלותך)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches that every journey of a Jew, summer vacation included, is a shlichus from Hashem, and that the hard days of Tamuz and Av, born of the spies' journey, hide the light of Moshiach for one who travels with kabbalas ol malchus shamayim.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the idea that every Jewish soul is a letter in the Torah, found in a parsha that matches its mission, and that some souls belong to parshiyos of wandering and exile, which is itself a tikkun. Pesach Sheni and Vayehi binsoa, both written out of place in Behaaloscha, show this. Citing the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'mei'Hashem mitzadei gever konanu', he explains that each step is set from Above, so a bochur in the mountains is sent to make a specific brachah. The yetzer hara is especially active in vacation time, so one must take on more ol malchus shamayim there, as the Torah's 'masa'os' are journeys of galus. He links the summer travel season to the spies' forty days in Tamuz and Av, days that hide great light and the birth of Moshiach. He closes with seeing Hashem in creation, the story of Reb Feivel's davening, and the power of tefillah that saved Kalev and Yehoshua.

en: Every Jew, family and generation has its own shlichus, and every soul is a letter in a parsha of the Torah connected to it.
Following the Ba'al Shem Tov, the Mashgiach teaches that a person's steps are fixed from Above, so every place he reaches holds a specific tikkun only he can do there.
Going to the country is no release from ol malchus shamayim; there the yetzer hara is stronger, so one must daven and learn better and accept more.
The travel season of Tamuz and Av corresponds to the spies' journey, and the Jewish people must repair that journey with their own.
The days of Tamuz and Av are hard, but they hide the light of Moshiach and are destined to become yomim tovim.
In the country one can see Hashem's creation clearly, and contemplating it should bring better davening and love of Hashem.

candidateTopics: Pesach Sheni and Vayehi binsoa out of place
the spies and the months of Tamuz and Av

title.en: Every soul a letter, every Jew a shlichus

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Behaaloscha and Shelach, parshiyos of journeys, and explains that each soul is a letter in a parsha that matches it, with its own shlichus. Souls that need repair find themselves in parshiyos of wandering, since galus is a great tikkun, as with Kayin.

title.en: Two parshiyos written out of place

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that the parsha of Pesach Sheni was moved from the start of Bamidbar so as not to shame Israel, and that Vayehi binsoa, per the Gemara in Shabbos, is also out of place and will return to its place when Moshiach comes. Both are parshiyos of souls in exile, and the summer travel season that begins with these parshiyos is no coincidence.

title.en: Steps fixed from Above: the brachah in the mountains

summary.en: Bringing the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'mei'Hashem mitzadei gever konanu', the Mashgiach explains that a bochur who makes a brachah on a berry or a drink from a stream in the mountains may be redeeming a soul that waited for him since creation. He tells of a tzaddik whose customer drank without a brachah on his father's yahrzeit, losing his father's soul's tikkun.

title.en: Clothing as ol malchus shamayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach warns that the yetzer hara is inventive, bringing the Ya'aros Devash on why people began wearing black on Shabbos. He explains that clothing casts a light of malchus shamayim on a person, which is why one adds garments for davening, and that shedding clothes in the country symbolizes throwing off the yoke; yet the Aron goes along on every journey.

title.en: A shlichus needs mesiras nefesh; the masa'os of galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach says one must be more careful in the country than at home, since a shlichus demands mesiras nefesh, as the Midrash contrasts Yehoshua's successful messengers with Moshe's spies. Through the Megaleh Amukos on 'Eleh masei', whose letters hint at the four exiles, he teaches that a Jew's journeys are journeys of galus, to be taken with kabbalas ol and not with a feeling of freedom.

title.en: Tamuz and Av: repairing the spies' journey

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the masa'os are read with the tune of the Shirah and recalls the Spanish exiles leaving with music, teaching that galus is to be walked with bitachon and the guidance of the leaders. He explains that the world travels in Tamuz and Av because the spies' forty days fell then, and reads the order of the camps' travel, Gershon and Merari, then the flags of Reuven and Shimon, then Gad, as a map of these months that ends in consolation.

title.en: The parsha of scattering and Reb Shimshon's warning

summary.en: After a Chelm joke about the pazer cantillation note, the Mashgiach points out that Behaaloscha is full of pazers, a parsha of scattering that prepares the people for Tamuz and Av. He brings Reb Shimshon of Ostropolia that the letters before 'anavim' in 'yemei bikurei anavim' spell the name of the Satan, which is why the spies fell in those days.

title.en: Adding the yud: hard days become holy

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Reb Shimshon's hint: the yud is missing, and where a Jew enters these days they become holy and will be the greatest yomim tovim, as Zechariah foretells. He adds that Moshe repaired Reuven, that Gad's count ending in fifty alludes to Eliyahu and the redemption, and that Hashem sends each one on a shlichus, to be like Yehoshua's messengers.

title.en: The two Ashreis and the forty-two journeys

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts 'Ashrei yoshvei veisecha' with 'Ashrei temimei derech', whose chapter ends with a lost sheep: being a Jew is easier at home, but when Hashem sends one on a journey one goes, guarding Hashem's charge. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov that every Jew passes through the forty-two journeys, warns of the pull of ballfields and pools, and says these days hold greater light.

title.en: Moshiach hidden in Tamuz and Av; grapes in the desert

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer that Boaz married Ruth on 17 Tamuz, the Midrash that Moshiach is born on Tisha B'Av, Aharon's 'chag laHashem machar', and the Kozhnitzer Maggid on 'bein hametzarim', to show that these days hide the light of Moshiach. Through Moshe's charge to take of the fruit and Hoshea's 'grapes in the desert', he explains that Hashem delights in a Jew who uses these days for His sake, while allowing exercise for health in measure, as the Rambam writes.

title.en: The spies' grapes as nesachim; the stars in the country

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash that the spies' cluster of grapes was used for nesachim, and Rashi that the parsha of nesachim comforted Israel after the spies, showing that the sin itself becomes the tikkun; Tamuz and Menachem Av, he adds, equal 'Melech HaMoshiach' in gematria. He then urges looking at the stars and sunsets in the country, as Yeshayahu says, and the Rambam's path to love of Hashem through contemplating creation, as Dovid HaMelech did.

title.en: Reb Feivel at the window; the tefillah that saved Kalev and Yehoshua

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how his rebbe Reb Feivel davened looking out the window and answered a critic that he was looking into Hashem's own writing, the world of Borchi Nafshi. He contrasts the city that hides Hashem's world with the country, where all creations sing shirah, then teaches that Kalev and Yehoshua were saved only through tefillah, and closes with a brachah for a summer of growth and for the fast days to become yomim tovim.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: שיחת פרידה - ברכות פרידה' לקדש שם שמים' להיות מעורב ונוח לבריות' לבנות ביהמ"ק ע"י אהבת חנם.

oneLiner.en: Parting from the bachurim before they leave for camp, the Mashgiach blesses them and asks them to sanctify Hashem's name through good conduct with others, warm tefillah and small daily acts that help complete the Beis Hamikdash.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the custom of Chazal to bless one another when parting from the yeshiva, citing the brachos in Gemara Berachos, including the wish that no talmid of the group turn out badly. From there he turns to the bachurim's time in camp among others: a ben Torah is watched, and bad middos or making things hard for roommates is a chillul Hashem, while good conduct makes him an example. He warns against showing off and pride, with a play on the name Devorah (a bee). He asks them to strengthen Torah and tefillah daily, to come on time and daven warmly, since kiddush Hashem is the greatest thing and chillul Hashem the worst. He brings the Sanzer Rav's teaching that the Beis Hamikdash is nearly complete, so small acts of self-restraint finish it, and a story of Reb Yechezkel'e of Kuzmir about ahavas chinam on Tisha B'Av. He closes with daily chizuk, like vitamin C, and blessings.

en: Chazal's custom was to bless one another when parting, and the Mashgiach applies their brachos to the bachurim leaving the yeshiva.
A ben Torah among others is watched, so bad middos or inconsiderate behavior is a chillul Hashem, while good conduct makes him an example for all.
Torah and tefillah need fresh chizuk every day, and a ben Torah should love rebuke and words of mussar.
Kiddush Hashem is the greatest thing there is, and its opposite, chillul Hashem, is not atoned even by Yom Kippur and suffering.
The Beis Hamikdash is nearly complete, and small acts of self-restraint, good learning and davening by each person help finish it.
Since the Beis Hamikdash was destroyed through sinas chinam, the main mourning today is ahavas chinam, doing a favor for another Jew.

candidateTopics: conduct of a ben Torah in camp
daily chizuk in Torah and tefillah
building the Beis Hamikdash through small deeds

title.en: Chazal's blessings when parting

summary.en: The Mashgiach takes leave of the bachurim, praising them, and explains that Chazal used to bless one another when leaving the yeshiva. He brings the brachos from Gemara Berachos, including the wish that no talmid of the group turn out like Achitofel, Doeg or Gechazi.

title.en: Kiddush Hashem among others in camp

summary.en: The Mashgiach warns that a ben Torah who goes out among others is watched: anger, a mess in a shared room or mockery is a chillul Hashem, while good middos make him an example. He warns against showing off group pride and against haughtiness, with a play on Devorah, whose name means bee.

title.en: Daily chizuk in Torah and tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Torah and tefillah need chizuk every day, that loving rebuke is one of the ways Torah is acquired, and asks the bachurim to come on time and daven warmly. Kiddush Hashem is the greatest thing, and chillul Hashem is not atoned even by Yom Kippur.

title.en: Small deeds finish the Beis Hamikdash

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Sanzer Rav's teaching that the heavenly Beis Hamikdash is complete except for the paroches, and his answer why he did not make it himself. Today only the smallest details remain, so small acts of restraint, not shaming others and good learning and davening, build it.

title.en: Ahavas chinam and the closing brachah

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how Reb Yechezkel'e of Kuzmir sent a weeping chassid on Tisha B'Av to do a favor for a Jew, since the churban came through sinas chinam. He asks the bachurim to help and encourage others, compares chizuk to vitamin C that must be taken daily, and blesses them.

title.en: The old chassidim's parting song

summary.en: The Mashgiach recalls how old Russian chassidim sang a niggun when parting from the Rebbe, about meeting again if Hashem grants life, followed by singing.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: להיות חלק מבריאה לעשות רצונו דרוש בפרק ר' אליעזר דמילה' נחיצות העבודה במחנה קיץ' חיזוק הרמת הקול בתפילה.

oneLiner.en: Speaking to bachurim about to leave for a summer camp, the Mashgiach explains that each of them is sent there as a shaliach of Hashem, like all of creation, and tells them to fulfill that mission by learning, avoiding machlokes, and davening warmly and aloud.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the summer months, when the meraglim went out, and says that every bachur going to camp is a shaliach meant to repair that sin. In the country one sees how trees, birds and water all do exactly what Hashem commanded at creation; a person should join this 'family' of creation, but by his own choice. He warns against machlokes, citing Korach, and contrasts it with machlokes for the sake of Heaven. He then introduces the perek of Rabbi Eliezer d'Milah: through the Eglei Tal and Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer he shows that milah and Shabbos are one matter, which is why hilchos milah are taught inside Maseches Shabbos. He stresses the danger that comes with a great mission, and closes with a long call, from the Ramban, the Ba'al haTanya and others, to daven together, with warmth and a raised voice.

en: Each bachur going to camp is a shaliach sent by Hashem, and the place, the rebbeim, the chaverim and the learning are the tools of that mission.
All of nature carries out the command Hashem gave it at creation; a person is asked to do the same, but through his own free choice.
Milah and Shabbos are one matter, each containing the whole Torah, so the laws of milah are taught within Maseches Shabbos.
The greater the mission, the greater the danger along the way, so one must strengthen oneself and guard against lashon hara, leitzanus and machlokes.
Davening aloud is a proclamation that we are Hashem's creations, and the voice arouses the heart, so the Mashgiach urges davening warmly and together, word by word.
Every tefillah is a diamond, as precious as Ne'ilah of Yom Kippur, and one who feels the pain cries out.

title.en: Going to camp as a shaliach

summary.en: The Mashgiach ties the summer to the time the meraglim set out, and says each bachur leaving home for camp is a shaliach meant to repair their sin. The rebbeim, chaverim, learning and davening are the tools of the mission, and at every step one chooses whether to be a faithful shaliach or like the meraglim.

title.en: All of creation does its shlichus

summary.en: In the country one sees the sky, grass, birds and water without buildings hiding them, each doing what Hashem commanded at creation. The Mashgiach asks why a person should be different, and says the bachurim should join this 'family of nature' as shluchim, but by choice, and work together as a team.

title.en: Korach and machlokes for Heaven's sake

summary.en: From Parshas Korach the Mashgiach teaches that one may not make machlokes like Korach and his company. He explains that their dispute was split inside as well, each wanting something else, because each sought himself; a machlokes of Torah for Heaven's sake instead brings friendship and team-work.

title.en: The Eglei Tal: Shabbos, milah and the Shach

summary.en: Introducing the perek of Rabbi Eliezer d'Milah, the Mashgiach brings the Eglei Tal's introduction: he wrote on hilchos Shabbos as a tikkun for pegam habris, since Shabbos contains the whole Torah. He then relates the Eglei Tal's defense of the Shach, who allows a transgression to save a limb, against the kal vachomer from milah in Yoma: milah overrides Shabbos only because it too contains everything.

title.en: Why hilchos milah are in Maseches Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that Shabbos and milah are both called bris and strengthen each other, and that all the laws of milah are taught through how milah falls on Shabbos. He asks why the perek opens with 'if he did not bring the tool' rather than with a new halacha, and answers that it continues the previous perek to show that hilchos milah are hilchos Shabbos.

title.en: Avraham's milah on Yom Kippur

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Avraham, who kept the whole Torah, waited for his milah until commanded, and answers from Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer that he was circumcised on Yom Kippur, the Shabbos of Shabbosos and root of Shabbos. He adds that milah is called the greatest mitzvah and pegam habris the greatest aveirah, and both are tied to Yom Kippur.

title.en: The worth of learning in camp

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every bit of Torah and every mitzvah of the smallest Jew raises the whole creation, and learning about milah is like fulfilling it. He urges the bachurim to use the precious time in camp with toil and chiddushim, and says that being sent to learn such Torah shows they are considered important in Heaven, like a president who sends only his best men on vital missions.

title.en: A great mission needs chizuk

summary.en: Like Moshe telling the meraglim to strengthen themselves, the Mashgiach says a precious mission is a dangerous one: a truck of diamonds needs armor and two drivers. The yetzer hara will lie in wait with lashon hara, leitzanus and machlokes, and just as the Gemara has a soul sworn and strengthened before birth, one must ask Hashem for chizuk and take only the good.

title.en: Avodas hatefillah and the Ramban

summary.en: Turning to tefillah, the Mashgiach says this generation must measure its davening against earlier ones and be ashamed of the weakness. Tefillah is avodah of the heart, and he brings the Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo: every mitzvah, even buying a mezuzah, rests on emunah, and the purpose of raising the voice in tefillah and of shuls is to proclaim publicly that we are Hashem's creations.

title.en: The Ba'al haTanya: daven together aloud

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ba'al haTanya, whose Shulchan Aruch is accepted everywhere, pleading that the tzibbur daven together word by word in a raised voice, not some loudly and others silently, as the Sefardim do. He adds that one asked by the gabbai to daven should not refuse, and that one with a fine voice must use it for Hashem, recalling Navos who withheld his voice.

title.en: The Pri Megadim and why we raise our voice

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the poskim on a loud voice: the Beis Yosef on answering with all one's strength, the Kaf HaChaim citing the Eliyahu Rabbah, and the Pri Megadim, brought by the Mishnah Berurah, that one need not shout since Hashem hears. He answers that the voice is not for Hashem to hear but to arouse kavanah and wake the sleeping neshamah; only one who needs no such arousal may daven quietly.

title.en: Levels of hidden avodah; the Chafetz Chaim

summary.en: From the Shunamis, who needed signs to know Elisha was holy, the Mashgiach explains that the higher a person stands, the less his avodah shows outside: yesharim sing and shout, tzaddikim less, chassidim and kedoshim hide it. He then brings the Chafetz Chaim, who writes that one should cry out to Hashem in tefillah, and the Stoliner Rebbe who davened aloud so chassidim would learn from him.

title.en: Every tefillah a Ne'ilah; closing charge

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks the bachurim to test for themselves whether they daven better with warmth, and notes that even a cold shul shouts at Ne'ilah, though every tefillah is a diamond. With the Gemara on Iyov, punished for keeping silent, he explains that one who feels the pain cries out. He closes with Shabbos Parshas Korach, the sweetness of Hodu on Erev Shabbos, and a brachah to be good shluchim.

catalogTitle: This שבת Finalizes פורים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parshas Parah, the Shabbos after Purim, continues Purim's lesson of a conduct above understanding, and that this is the merit through which Hashem can bring the Geulah in Nisan despite the Satan's accusations.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Parshas Parah as the last Shabbos of the old year and explains that Haman erred in thinking Adar was the end, since for Jews the end touches the beginning. The sin of the Eitz HaDaas was the demand to understand everything; Parah Adumah, a chok that even Shlomo HaMelech could not understand, repairs it and partly atones for the Egel. Purim reflects Hashem's conduct with Jews as children, which is beyond reason, and Parah continues it. Turning to the year 5760, he explains the difference between a year fit for redemption and the fixed final time, describes how the Satan's accusations brought the decrees of Tach v'Tat and the world wars, and urges teshuvah. Parshas Parah, read before Nisan and before the three weeks, answers the Satan. Through the Gemara in Yoma about the race to the Mizbeach and the lottery, he shows that the goral reflects a conduct beyond merits. He closes with the higher purity of sprinkled water that comes from above.

en: For Jews time runs in a circle, so the end of the year touches its beginning; Haman, who rejoiced that his lot fell on Adar, did not understand this.
The sin of the Eitz HaDaas was the insistence on understanding everything, and Parah Adumah, a mitzvah kept without understanding, is its repair.
Hashem leads the Jews either as servants, according to their deeds, or as children, unconditionally; the miracle of Purim came through the conduct of children, which is above understanding.
When a time fit for Geulah arrives, the Satan accuses the Jews of their sins, and if they are not worthy, troubles come instead.
Parshas Parah is read before Nisan, a time of chesed, and Parshas Chukas before the three weeks, a time of rachamim, to answer the Satan's reasoning with a mitzvah done without reasons.
A goral reflects a conduct above merits; in the Beis HaMikdash a tie in the race showed that on that day the conduct was as children, so all the kohanim entered the lottery.
Parah Adumah brings a purity that comes from above, without the person's own act, and on Shabbos Parshas Parah Hashem grants every Jew a purity of the soul in preparation for Nisan.

candidateTopics: Parah Adumah as a chok beyond understanding
Hashem's conduct with Jews as children and as servants

title.en: The last Shabbos of the year and Haman's error

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Shabbos feeds the coming week and that Parshas Parah is the last Shabbos of the old year. Haman rejoiced that his lot fell on Adar, the end, but for Jews the end touches the beginning like a circle. He then defines the sin of the Eitz HaDaas as the wish to understand everything.

title.en: Parah Adumah, a mitzvah beyond understanding

summary.en: The Mashgiach presents Parah Adumah as the one mitzvah that teaches not to expect to understand, which even Shlomo HaMelech could not grasp. He explains that the Eitz HaDaas brought death, Matan Torah removed it, and the Egel, the same sin of wanting to understand, brought it back; Parah atones for the Egel partially by removing tumas meis.

title.en: Purim: Hashem's conduct with His children

summary.en: The Mashgiach distinguishes Hashem's two ways of leading the Jews, as servants and as children, and explains that the miracle of Purim came not through merit but because Jews are children of Hashem. Since this bond is above reason, Purim calls for surrendering one's da'as, and Parah, which follows Purim, continues it.

title.en: A year fit for Geulah and the fixed time

summary.en: The Mashgiach defines emunah as believing what one does not understand and calls the year 5760 especially fit for Moshiach. Through the passuk 'b'itah achishenah' he distinguishes years that are fit for Geulah from the fixed final time that no prophet may know, which was hidden even from Yaakov Avinu, and he explains that at every such time the Satan accuses the Jews.

title.en: Missed years of redemption and the call to teshuvah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the decrees of Tach v'Tat, the Malbim's calculation for 1914 when the First World War began, and the expectation for the year Tav-Shin when the Second World War started, which he remembers from his boyhood. He points to this year's many tragedies as signs of the Satan's accusation and calls for Torah, teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.

title.en: Parah answers the Satan before Nisan and the three weeks

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Satan argues there is no reason to bring Moshiach, and the answer is a mitzvah that itself has no reason, Parah. Nisan, a time of Geulah through chesed, and the three weeks, a time of rachamim through the Churban, are each preceded by the reading of Parah, so that Hashem may bring the Geulah without reasons.

title.en: The goral and the race to the Mizbeach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Purim miracle came through a goral, which like a lottery win cannot be explained. He brings the Gemara in Yoma on the kohanim racing up the Mizbeach and the lottery after a tie, and asks why all the kohanim enter the lottery and how a race could decide the avodah. From Koheles he answers that in the Beis HaMikdash there was no hester panim, so whoever reached first did so through merit.

title.en: A tie shows a day of children; Parah after Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how two kohanim can arrive together when no two Jews are on the same level, and answers that a tie shows that on that day Hashem was leading as with children, beyond merits, so a goral decides. Parshas Parah, the Shabbos after Purim, uses this same root of the goral before Nisan, and he begins to distinguish purity of the body from purity of the soul.

title.en: Purity sprinkled from above

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that whoever hears Parshas Parah receives a purity of the soul from Hashem, preparing him for the Korban Pesach. He contrasts the mikveh, which requires one's own act and cannot remove tumas meis, with the water of Parah, sprinkled from above, which can, and he closes by asking listeners to stand ready with humility and teshuvah when the parshah is read.

catalogTitle: חיזוק בתפילה: לעשות ריח ניחוח לה'' בא אתה וכל ביתך אל התיבה' רמב"ן פרשת בא' אגרות מבעל התניא ורבי ר' יונתן בעניני תפילה.

oneLiner.en: On Shiva Asar b'Tammuz, when the korban tamid ceased, the Mashgiach calls for tefilah that is a 're'ach nichoach' to Hashem: davening with one's whole self, aloud, at length and together with the tzibbur, as the teivah that saves from the flood of the last generations.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Shiva Asar b'Tammuz: the breaking of the luchos brought forgetfulness, so familiar things must be repeated, and since the tamid ceased, our tefillos stand in its place and must be a 're'ach nichoach'. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's reading of 'tzohar ta'aseh lateivah': a person must enter the teivah, the word of tefilah, with his whole self, for tefilah is Noach's ark against the flood of desires and heresy before Moshiach. He contrasts Torah and tefilah: learning wins honor while long davening is mocked, as the Gemara foresaw. From the Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo he shows that the purpose of creation is that people gather and proclaim before Hashem, and so tefilah needs a voice. He reads letters of the Ba'al HaTanya and Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz, tells stories about lateness and loud davening, describes the heichalos of pesukei dezimra, and closes with warnings against leitzanus and politics and a call to ahavas chaverim.

en: Since the tamid ceased, tefillah stands in its place, so a Jew's davening must itself be a 're'ach nichoach' that pleases Hashem.
Tefilah is Noach's teivah: the world is a flood of desires, and before Moshiach a flood of heresy, and one is saved by entering the words of davening with one's whole being.
Torah and tefilah need each other, yet people honor learning and mock long davening, which the Gemara calls a thing that stands at the height of the world and is treated lightly.
Following the Ramban, the purpose of creation and of the shul is that people gather to proclaim before Hashem that they are His creations, and so tefilah needs a voice.
Based on the Ba'al HaTanya's letters, the Mashgiach teaches that davening should take its time, pesukei dezimra should be said together with the tzibbur, and the ba'al tefilah should not be rushed.
Each chapter and each word of davening is a heichal above, and one who says it together with the tzibbur enters the heichal with them.
In today's new trials the yeshiva is the place to flee to, and within it one must flee leitzanus and politics and hold on to ahavas chaverim.

candidateTopics: tefilah in place of the korban tamid
the teivah of tefilah and the flood

title.en: Forgetting, the tamid and a re'ach nichoach

summary.en: The Mashgiach connects Shiva Asar b'Tammuz to the breaking of the luchos, which brought forgetfulness, and explains why things already heard must be repeated. Since the tamid ceased that day and tefillos stand in place of the tamid, he asks how our davening can be a 're'ach nichoach' for Hashem.

title.en: The teivah of tefilah against the flood

summary.en: After a self-deprecating mashal of a bus driver, the Mashgiach brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'tzohar ta'aseh lateivah' and 'bo atah vechol beischa el hateivah': enter the word of tefilah with your whole self. Tefilah is the teivah that saves from the flood of desires and, before Moshiach, of heresy, and it is the defense against Amalek, who attacks the weak souls.

title.en: Torah and tefilah, and why davening is mocked

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Torah, the service of the mind, with tefilah, the service of the heart, and tells how the beis medrash was founded so that bochurim could keep davening as warmly as in camp. He insists Torah and tefilah need each other, then asks why learning brings honor while long davening is laughed at, and answers with the Gemara on things that stand at the height of the world.

title.en: The Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo: the purpose of creation is that man thank and acknowledge his Creator, and this is the purpose of shuls and of tefilah b'tzibbur, to gather and proclaim 'we are Your creations'. Through the Ramban he brings that tefilah needs a voice, 'chutzpah natzach l'bisha', overcoming the yetzer hara.

title.en: Why daven aloud

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers those who mock loud davening: they themselves shout at Ne'ilah, and every tefilah should be a Ne'ilah. Only tzaddikim can daven quietly, as Rabbi Aharon of Karlin says; others must outshout the yetzer hara, which is itself loud, and he brings the Boyaner Rebbe's word that nowadays one must daven aloud with hislahavus.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya's letters on davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the Ba'al HaTanya's letters: weekday davening should take about an hour and a half, businessmen must not rush the ba'al tefilah, and the long daveners should stand around him. He brings the Chasam Sofer's long davening as a bochur, the Gemara that one who lengthens his tefilah has his days lengthened, the teaching that in the time before Moshiach the main thing is tefilah, and the Ba'al HaTanya's plea that pesukei dezimra be said together, word by word.

title.en: Rabbi Aharon of Karlin and Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how Rabbi Aharon of Karlin, called before a beis din for shouting in davening, answered that when a house burns one shouts. He then reads Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz's letter in Yaaros Devash: the young men laughed at his long Shemoneh Esrei, yet his portion from all his toil was the moments he stood before Hashem in tefilah.

title.en: Coming late: Bilgah and the late neshamah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara at the end of Sukkah about the mishmar of Bilgah, whose ring was sealed because they came late, a sign the avodah was not dear to them, and compares it to a heart bypass. He then tells from Meir Einei HaGolah how a neshamah came to the Chidushei HaRim for a tikkun after the candles were lit, too late, because in its lifetime it came late to davening.

title.en: The heichalos of davening with the tzibbur

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why pesukei dezimra is said together: each chapter of Tehillim, and each word, is a heichal that opens only with the tzibbur. He goes through Shiras HaYam as a cheap segulah, Ahavah Rabbah, Emes Veyatziv and the descent of shefa after Shemoneh Esrei, with a mashal of paying for a watch and leaving without it, and then speaks of the ba'al tefilah who must lift the people and of learning as preparation for davening.

title.en: Fleeing into the yeshiva, and fleeing leitzanus

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the new temptations of today's inventions and the dangers of the street, and tells how the Satmar Rav, citing the Rambam that one should flee bad surroundings even to the desert, said that today one flees into the yeshiva. Inside the yeshiva too one must know whom to flee, above all a fixed habit of leitzanus, which uproots emunah.

title.en: Politics, ahavas chaverim and a closing tefilah

summary.en: The Mashgiach warns against any involvement in politics and machlokes, then calls for ahavas chaverim, good friends who help and strengthen one another, as a foundation the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Arizal planted, and as a cure for the forces of Shiva Asar b'Tammuz. He closes with a tefilah for the rebuilding of Yerushalayim.

catalogTitle: סעודת הודאה: צריכים להודות לה' על כל נשימה ונשימה (צוואת יסוד ושורש העבודה)

oneLiner.en: At a seudas hodaah in Kislev, the Mashgiach teaches that a Jew must thank Hashem for every breath and every small detail, drawing on the will of the author of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah, and ends with the special thanks of a Jewish mother.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Kislev as the month of hodaah, the Chanukah days set for Hallel and thanks. He explains Modim d'Rabbanan, where we thank Hashem for putting into our hearts the wish to thank Him, and the four people who must thank. From Dovid Hamelech's closing words, 'kol haneshamah', he learns that one must thank for every breath. He then reads from the will at the end of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah, whose author thanked Hashem aloud for a private room, warm clothes, a snuffbox that did not spill and glasses that did not break, and calls this an exercise in emunah. The four who must thank are only examples for the wise man to learn from; two of the ten must be rabbanan, because the second finds what the first left out. He applies this to the seudah, to the beis medrash and to Kislev, and ends with the mother's mesirus nefesh, the hidden heart of the miracle, and Leah's thanks for a child.

en: Since everything that happens to a person comes from Hashem with hashgachah pratis, he must thank Him for every pleasure, large or small.
The verse 'kol haneshamah' teaches, as Chazal expound it, that one must thank Hashem for every single breath.
The will of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah shows a Jew who thanked Hashem aloud, with joy, for each small kindness of his day.
The four who must thank are only headings; a wise man learns from them that there are hidden miracles every day, beginning with the workings of the body.
Hodaah is never finished, which is why two of the ten at a seudas hodaah must be rabbanan and why everyone adds his own Modim d'Rabbanan.
The hidden heart of the miracles of Yetzias Mitzrayim and Chanukah was the mesirus nefesh of righteous women, and a mother's thanks for a child is a thanks of its own kind.

title.en: Kislev, Modim and the four who must thank

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens the seudas hodaah by calling Kislev the month of hodaah, explains Rashi on Modim d'Rabbanan that we thank Hashem for letting us thank, and asks why the Gemara gives the congregation its own text at Modim. He then brings the four who must thank and the rule that the thanks be said before ten, two of them rabbanan.

title.en: Thanks for every breath; the will of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah

summary.en: From the end of Tehillim, 'kol haneshamah', the Mashgiach learns that one must thank for every breath. He introduces the author of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah, whose avodah the Chozeh of Lublin praised, and his will, written to teach his children rather than to boast.

title.en: Reading the will: thanks for each small kindness

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads one item after another from the will: the author's thanks for a private room for avodah, for news of his children's health, for Shabbos clothes, a warm winter coat, answering Kedushah, having a needed item and the money for it, and for a fallen snuffbox, bottle and glasses that did not break. He calls this an exercise in emunah and adds that one must thank even when a shoelace does not tear.

title.en: The four are only examples: hidden daily miracles

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the four who must thank are only headings: Hashem does great wonders 'alone', hidden ones no one sees. He describes the body's many systems, more delicate than a car of steel, and says that 'mi chacham' teaches a wise man to learn from the four to everything.

title.en: Why two rabbanan, and why Modim d'Rabbanan

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why two of the ten must be rabbanan and answers that the second chacham shows that after the first has finished there is still more to thank for, as Nishmas says. With this he answers his opening question: for hodaah the chazzan's words are not enough, so each one says Modim d'Rabbanan.

title.en: Korban todah, seudas hodaah and tonight's simcha

summary.en: Without a Beis Hamikdash, the seudas hodaah takes the place of the korban todah. The Mashgiach brings the mefarshim on why the todah is eaten only for a day and a night: to bring more people and spread the thanks. He then names tonight's thanks for a child who came home well, to the doctors' wonder.

title.en: Thanks for the beis medrash and for every toothpick

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the chaburah must thank Hashem for a beis medrash of serious ovdei Hashem with a warm, good davening, rare in today's cold times, and should use that gift. As Kislev comes, he urges taking on to thank for every detail, even a toothpick, as a fruit of emunah, hashgachah pratis and bitachon.

title.en: Thanking mothers: the hidden heart of the miracle

summary.en: The Mashgiach praises the Oberland custom of thanking the mother after a meal and brings the Gemara that Leah was the first to thank Hashem. Through the Rashbam, that women were the main cause of the miracle, and Tosafos' question on him, he explains that the women's mesirus nefesh in Mitzrayim was the hidden heart of the redemption while Moshe and Aharon led openly.

title.en: Leah's thanks for a child; closing brachah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Leah, who already had three children, thanked for another as a mother building Klal Yisroel, a new kind of thanks; such is a mother's devotion at her child's hospital bed. He ties this to Chanukah, then blesses that all Jews thank Hashem together at the redemption, when even the galus will be understood as kindness.

catalogTitle: מטרת החסידות: לעבודת ה' ולאהבת חברים ולא להתחלק למפלגות.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches that the task of the generation before Moshiach is to serve Hashem with emes, and that true chassidus means love of friends and of every Jew rather than splitting into rival camps.

abstract.en: Speaking to a group of young men gathered to grow in fear of Heaven, the Mashgiach notes that emes is the last word of Krias Shema, corresponding to the heel, the lowest generation before Moshiach. Emes is not written in the Torah's text; each generation must add it, and this generation's task is emes, though the Gemara says truth will then be missing. Truth is one, so when it becomes 'flocks and flocks', each group with its own truth, that is falsehood. The Ba'al Shem Tov built chassidus on emes, but its strength has faded. Reading from Shomer Emunim, the Mashgiach explains that the essence of chassidus is love of the tzaddik, of friends and of all Jews; each group has its own root, but hating another group is the work of the Satan. Friends who share a root must care for one another, and even thinking badly of a friend, as a story of the Ba'al Shem Tov shows, gives power to the accuser.

en: Emes, the last word of Krias Shema, corresponds to the heel, the generation of ikvesa d'meshicha, whose task is to bring emes.
Truth is only one; when every group has its own 'truth', as in 'the truth will become flocks and flocks', it is not truth.
The work of today is to serve Hashem with emes, not for other motives.
The essence of chassidus is love of the tzaddik, of friends and of all Jews; division between chassidic groups is falsehood and the Satan's work.
Each group may have its own Rebbe according to its root, but one must love a fellow Jew even if he follows a different Rebbe.
Those who sit together share one root of soul and must care for one another first, while still loving every Jew.
Thinking badly of a fellow Jew is even worse than speaking badly, because thought reaches higher.

the derech of the Ba'al Shem Tov

title.en: Emes, the last word of Krias Shema

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Yaakov Avinu and the attribute of emes. Each of the 248 words of Krias Shema corresponds to a limb, so the last word, emes, corresponds to the heel, which the Tanya compares to the lowest generation, ikvesa d'meshicha.

title.en: Our generation must add the emes

summary.en: The word emes is not in the Torah's parsha of Shema; we add it ourselves, because each generation has its task and the last generation's task is emes. He brings that before Moshiach truth will be missing, that emes is Hashem's seal, and that truth is only one, so 'flocks and flocks' of truths are not truth, illustrated with the time on a clock.

title.en: Chassidus built on emes, and its decline

summary.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov built chassidus on the attribute of emes, but falsehood will spread before Moshiach, so the work of young and old today is to serve Hashem with emes. Starting to read from Shomer Emunim, he describes the 150 years of the Ba'al Shem Tov's way, its great tzaddikim, and how it weakened, especially after the two world wars, leaving only an impression to hold on to.

title.en: The essence of chassidus: love of friends

summary.en: From Shomer Emunim the Mashgiach reads that the essence of chassidus is love of the tzaddik, of friends and of all Israel, and that there must be peace between the chassidic groups. With the Chasam Sofer's twelve tribes and twelve gates, and the Sefardim and Ashkenazim following the Mechaber and the Rema, he explains that each root may have its own way and its own Rebbe.

title.en: Belonging to a team

summary.en: Bringing the Steipler, the Mashgiach explains that every person wants to be great, and one who cannot becomes great through his team, like fans of ball teams. Chassidus today is often treated the same way; the Sanzer Rav rejected chassidim claiming their Rebbe is greater, and Shomer Emunim says hating a Jew because he is not of one's chassidim is not chassidus.

title.en: All hatred is falsehood

summary.en: Continuing Shomer Emunim, the Mashgiach reads that one must love every Jew, especially those who keep mitzvos, and in this dark generation kiss the feet of every true believer. Every hatred is falsehood and the Satan's doing; the Ba'al Shem Tov, the greatest lover of Israel, never meant his way to divide Jews. This, the Mashgiach says, is the truth that has become 'flocks and flocks'.

title.en: Those near in soul come first

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells his listeners that they did not sit together by chance: they share one root of soul and stood near each other at Har Sinai. Like a relative who comes first for tzedakah, those close to one come first, yet every Jew must be loved. Serving Hashem with emes means loving Hashem, Jews and Torah; each Jew is a letter of the Sefer Torah and each group a parsha, all bound together.

title.en: Caring for a friend, and the snuff story

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes love of friends in practice: caring about a friend's situation, davening and collecting money for him, joining his simcha and comforting him, and accepting the mitzvah of loving one's fellow before davening, as the Arizal says. He tells of a disciple of the Ba'al Shem Tov who was disturbed that a friend took snuff during davening, until he understood the friend needed it for strength, and was later told he had been an accuser.

title.en: Thought reaches higher than speech

summary.en: From the Chofetz Chaim the Mashgiach explains that speaking against a Jew gives strength to the accuser above, and chassidic sefarim read 'do not join hands with the wicked' this way. Thinking badly is even worse, since thought reaches higher worlds than speech and deed; so one should think, speak and act well toward others, especially friends of one's root. He closes hoping to continue on love of friends another time.

catalogTitle: Our Waiting and Preparation for the Ultimate ניסן of Creation

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Nisan is an offshoot of the original Rosh Chodesh Nisan of Creation, which Hashem has tried to bring down again and again, and that a Jew should renew himself and pray that this Nisan be the one of the final redemption.

abstract.en: Opening with Parshas HaChodesh, the Mashgiach calls Nisan a month of pure chesed and love between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, which is why Shir HaShirim is said on Pesach. Adam was created on Rosh Chodesh Nisan, meant to enter an everlasting Shabbos, but the Satan spoiled the plan; in human terms Hashem was disappointed. Like a soul returning as a gilgul or ibbur, that original Nisan came down again at Yetzias Mitzrayim and was spoiled by the Eigel, and again at the Mishkan's inauguration, spoiled once more. The Nisan of the Geulah is still awaited. He urges bentching Rosh Chodesh Nisan with kavanah, staying away from machlokes and keeping a kosher Pesach. Pesach belongs to Avraham and binds a Jew to Hashem, as kareis on Pesach and milah shows. Through gematria he shows that matzah is 'three times Adam'. As nature renews itself in Nisan, a Jew should renew himself and crown Hashem.

en: The chesed felt in the world every Nisan is a byproduct of the real Nisan, the love of Hashem for Klal Yisrael like a groom for a bride.
Adam was created on Rosh Chodesh Nisan so that he would pass from Friday into an everlasting Shabbos, and the Satan's sin spoiled that original 'Nisan of Bereishis'.
Like a gilgul or an ibbur of a soul, the original Nisan was brought down again at Yetzias Mitzrayim and at the inauguration of the Mishkan, and both times it was spoiled.
Klal Yisrael is still waiting for the original Nisan to come down once more as the Nisan of the Geulah.
Pesach belongs to Avraham Avinu and is the moment a Jew binds himself to Hashem, which is why kareis applies to the positive mitzvos of milah and korban Pesach.
Matzah carries kedushah like tzitzis made for the sake of the mitzvah, and its value is 'lechem' with the full spelling of Hashem's Name: three times the Adam of 'na'aseh adam'.
Since all of nature renews itself in Nisan, a Jew should renew himself too and resolve to become a true Adam.

candidateTopics: Nisan as a month of chesed

title.en: Nisan, a month of chesed and love

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Parshas HaChodesh and describes Nisan as a month of pure chesed that is felt even in nature. He explains that this is a byproduct of the real Nisan, Hashem's love for Klal Yisrael like a groom's for a bride, which is why Shir HaShirim is said on Pesach.

title.en: The Nisan of Creation and its spoiling

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Adam was created on Rosh Chodesh Nisan, the sixth day of Creation, to enter an everlasting Shabbos, and that the Satan spoiled this plan through the sin. He asks how one can speak of Hashem being disappointed and answers that this is only how humans can describe it.

title.en: Gilgul and ibbur: a soul that returns

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Hashem decided to bring the original Nisan down again, and explains the difference between a gilgul and an ibbur, where a tzaddik's soul enters a person to help him. He illustrates it with an unexpectedly elevated Shabbos after the mikveh and with the story of the Arizal standing up for Rabbi Chaim Vital.

title.en: The second try: Nisan of Yetzias Mitzrayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that place, time and soul all mirror each other, so an ibbur exists in place and in time too, as when the kedushah of Yerushalayim came to the Jews in the desert. The Nisan of Bereishis came down again at Yetzias Mitzrayim and rose until the Eigel spoiled it and death returned.

title.en: The Mishkan, and the Nisan still awaited

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the third try, the Nisan of the Mishkan's inauguration that is read about this week, which would have restored the state of Adam before the sin but was also spoiled. He stresses that Hashem never truly fails, and that the original Nisan will come down once more as the Nisan of the Geulah.

title.en: Bentching Rosh Chodesh Nisan; avoiding machlokes

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks that Rosh Chodesh Nisan be bentched this Shabbos with full kavanah, that it be the promised Nisan of the Geulah, especially in the year 5760. He warns at length to have no part in the current machlokes, and to learn, daven, give tzedakah, keep Shabbos and make a kosher Pesach.

title.en: Pesach, Avraham Avinu and the bond of matzah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Pesach is the yom tov of Avraham Avinu, as Shavuos is Yitzchak's and Sukkos Yaakov's, and that through Pesach a Jew becomes a Jew and binds himself to Hashem. This is why only milah and korban Pesach carry kareis among positive mitzvos, and why matzah, baked for the sake of the mitzvah, is filled with kedushah like tzitzis.

title.en: Matzah: three times Adam

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that lechem is 78, three times Hashem's Name, and that matzah is the same 'lechem' with the full spelling of the Name, three times 45, the gematria of Adam. Eating matzah with kavanah and emunah fulfills 'na'aseh adam' at least in the individual, and he adds that there is far more to every mitzvah than appears on the surface.

title.en: Renew yourself; crown Hashem as King

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how all of nature comes back to life in Nisan and sings to Hashem, and calls on each Jew not to sit back but to renew himself and resolve to become an Adam, as everything is new on Pesach. He closes with Nisan as the new year for kings and the roshei teivos of Hashem's Name, and prays that this Nisan be the Nisan of the Geulah.

catalogTitle: Cell Phones: בענין קליפת "תכבד העבודה" בזמן הזה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Pharaoh's decree 'let the work be made heavier' lives on today as a klipah of constant busyness, from phones and cell phones to social obligations and lavish simchas, that robs a Jew of any moment of calm reflection.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying he will repeat familiar things, as the Mesilas Yesharim says, because they need constant reminding. Following Reb Elchonon Wasserman, he presents the exile in Egypt as a model of today's exile: its last stretch was the hardest. When the Jews gathered on Shabbos to read scrolls promising redemption, Pharaoh decreed 'tichbad ha'avodah' so they would have no time to draw hope. Egypt was a 'house of slaves', a culture of work without thought. In Europe Jews were forced to toil, and a weary sigh at Minchah was precious; in America people choose the burden. Inventions save time, but the klipah fills it with new burdens: the telephone, then the cell phone, ringing in the beis medrash, and social pressures like kiddushes, nightly sheva brachos and costly weddings. He calls on each person to leave this Egypt and promises calm and joy from Heaven.

en: The Egyptian exile is a model of today's exile, and its final, hardest stage was Pharaoh's decree to make the work heavier.
Pharaoh's aim was to leave the Jews no time for the Shabbos gatherings where they drew hope from their scrolls of redemption.
Today too there is a klipah of 'tichbad ha'avodah': people are so busy and exhausted that they have no moment of yishuv hadaas to ask what they are doing in the world.
A Jew in Europe who was forced to toil was precious to Hashem, but one who chooses the burden in America is at fault.
Inventions save time, but the klipah fills the saved time with new burdens, above all the telephone and the cell phone.
Social pressures such as many kiddushes, nightly sheva brachos and lavish weddings are also part of this klipah, and one is not obligated to follow them.
Each person must decide to leave this Egypt, and one who frees himself is given calm and joy from Heaven.
