title.en: Sukkos as a return to Gan Eden

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Sukkos the strength of the whole year and explains that after Yom Kippur atones for Adam's sin, Jews are let back into the Garden of Eden, a place of joy. He introduces Hoshana Rabbah and Shemini Atzeres as the days of David and Shlomo, a likeness of the days of Moshiach.

title.en: Shemini Atzeres and Vezos Habracha

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Shemini Atzeres is the peak of all the Yamim Tovim and is not called a chag, and that reaching it needs a teshuvah greater than Yom Kippur. He brings Reb Pinchas of Koretz on why Vezos Habracha is not counted among the Shabbos parshiyos, and explains that it belongs to a higher Shabbos.

title.en: The structure of parshas Re'eh

summary.en: The Mashgiach surveys parshas Re'eh: it opens with eating before Hashem in Yerushalayim, turns to the meisis, the ir hanidachas and the forbidden animals, then returns to aser te'aser. He asks why the Torah does not join the beginning to the end, and begins to answer that eating is the gravest of acts, as the sin of the Eitz Hadaas shows.

title.en: Timtum halev and the four klipos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that food becomes part of a person and forbidden food dulls the heart. He links Yechezkel's four klipos to the four exiles and the four impure animals, with the chazir as Edom, and contrasts the upright of heart who feel their bond with Hashem, which every Jew can reach in moments of dveikus.

title.en: Feeling the bond: the bas Levi and the Lechovitcher

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Avnei Nezer on why a bas Levi who remarried on a single witness and was mistaken loses terumah: a wife feels her bond with her husband, and so the tribe of Levi felt its bond with Hashem. He tells how the Lechovitcher sensed his rebbe's passing, and reads Baal Peor and 've'atem hadveikim' the same way.

title.en: The meisis and forbidden food

summary.en: Returning to Re'eh, the Mashgiach explains that holy eating binds a Jew to Hashem, and one who feels that bond cannot be swayed by a false prophet; the Torah then sets the forbidden animals right after the meisis. He brings the Toldos Yaakov Yosef's story from the Ba'al Shem Tov about the Rambam and those who questioned techiyas hameisim.

title.en: How did you fall? Lo sochal kol to'eivah

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the Torah after the meisis as crying out to the fallen Jew how he lost his dveikus, and answering: lo sochal kol to'eivah. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar in Igra DePirka from Reb Mendel of Rimanov on children who go off because of their parents' food, and the Bnei Yissaschar's conclusion that this is no excuse and one can purify himself.

title.en: Aser te'aser as the repair; the Shabbos meal

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the order of Re'eh: the opening speaks of an upright Jew, the middle of the damage of forbidden food, and the closing aser te'aser of the one who breaks through with teshuvah. He brings Reb Nachman's saying that one who believes he can damage must believe he can repair, and the Chiddushei HaRim that the Shabbos meal is a meal of emunah.

title.en: Holy places; the chazir as the last exile

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Reb Shalom of Belz that the air of the Beis Hamikdash is in the sukkah, and calls the beis medrash a holy place. He explains that the chazir is the worst of the four animals because it is Edom, the present exile, and brings the Midrash and a Shabbos zemer on the separate verse for it. He then brings the Gemara on the number of aliyos by the measure of bittul melacha.

title.en: Rosh Chodesh, women and the curse of melacha

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi and Tosafos that women refrain from work on Rosh Chodesh because they did not give their jewelry to the egel, and the Tzlach's question why there are four aliyos when the men work. He explains that melacha is a curse that came from Adam's eating, that days of brachah such as Shabbos and Yom Tov are free of it, and that the women's brachah on Rosh Chodesh spreads to their husbands.

title.en: Days of brachah; why women merited Rosh Chodesh

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that kohanim, Yerushalayim, shemitah and a chassan and kallah are bound up with brachah and kept from melacha. He brings Reb Tzadok that Rosh Chodesh will be holier than Shabbos in the future, and the Baal HaTanya on matzah as daas and wine as feeling, and concludes that women, who felt the bond at the egel, merited Rosh Chodesh, which needs that feeling; he adds David and Shaul's seudah.

title.en: The repair: holy eating at home

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that even those who ate forbidden food in times of persecution on a rav's ruling still carry timtum halev, and its repair is holy eating in a holy place. He explains that after Shemini Atzeres the sukkah goes into the home, and describes the Shabbos table, netilas yadayim and bentching with kavanah from a siddur, bringing the Mishnah Berurah, the Rokeach and the Sefer HaChinuch.

title.en: Shemini Atzeres: love, teshuvah and protection

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Shemini Atzeres a day of pure love when the heart opens to Hashem, brings Reb Shalom of Belz and the Minchas Elazar on davening with kavanah on these three days, and explains that this teshuvah with the whole heart is why aser te'aser is read then. He closes with the sukkah as protection for all Jews and the world, and a brachah.

catalogTitle: מוצאי שמיטה: במוצאי שביעית בן דוד בא; כי שנה השמינית הוא בחינת לעתיד לבא

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that after the seven of shemitah comes the 'eighth', a glimpse of yovel and the world of Moshiach, which is why the Gemara says Moshiach comes at the end of shemitah and why the Rosh Hashanah and Hakhel after shemitah carry a special hope.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the mitzvah of appointing a king, asking why asking Shmuel for a king was resented. Turning to the Elul after shemitah and the coming Hakhel, he reviews that Yerushalayim is a permanent shemitah, and that shemitah is its overflow over all of Eretz Yisrael, so shemitah is entirely tosefes; this explains why the law of tosefes is learned from shemitah, and by Rabbi Akiva. Yovel, Shavuos and Yom Kippur are the 'eighth', above the seven days of nature, as the Maharal writes about Chanukah and milah. The Kodesh HaKodashim is where heaven meets earth, so the aron took no space. The end of Shabbos and of shemitah touches the eighth, hence melave malka, Moshiach coming after shemitah, and Hakhel. Children are brought to Hakhel in hope of singing shirah, and no waiting for Moshiach is wasted. He closes urging all to accept Hashem as King.

en: Yerushalayim is a constant shemitah; in the seventh year its 'spring' overflows over all of Eretz Yisrael and every Jew becomes like a kohen.
All of shemitah is tosefes on Yerushalayim, which is why the halachah of tosefes is learned from shemitah rather than from Shabbos or Yom Kippur.
The 'eighth' level, yovel, Shavuos, Yom Kippur and the Kodesh HaKodashim, stands above the seven days of creation and belongs to the days of Moshiach.
At the end of every Shabbos and every shemitah the eighth draws near, which is why Moshiach is expected after shemitah and why melave malka is David's meal.
Hakhel in the eighth year joins the king, the heart of the nation, with Yerushalayim, the heart of place, and is a time when the eighth world may be revealed.
No Jew's waiting for Moshiach is wasted; every hope joins the waiting of all generations and brings Moshiach closer.

title.en: Why asking Shmuel for a king was resented

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the parsha of appointing a king and the Rambam that it is a mitzvah, and asks why the request to Shmuel was resented. He notes from the Gemara about Shaul that Shmuel already functioned as king, and asks why they did not simply appoint him.

title.en: Elul after shemitah and the coming Hakhel

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that it is Elul at the end of shemitah, with Hakhel due on Sukkos. He brings the Chasam Sofer that after a year of Torah the Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Sukkos are greater, and says that to understand Hakhel one must understand shemitah and yovel.

title.en: Yerushalayim as a constant shemitah

summary.en: Reviewing an earlier year's shiur, the Mashgiach explains that Yerushalayim is always in a state of shemitah: Torah study, hefker, no planting, no tribal ownership, the city of kohanim. In the seventh year this overflows over all of Eretz Yisrael and every Jew becomes like a kohen.

title.en: Tosefes is learned from shemitah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Rabbi Akiva learns tosefes from the extra verse about plowing and harvest, said of shemitah, and asks why it is not learned from Yom Kippur. He answers that shemitah itself is tosefes on Yerushalayim, and explains why it is specifically Rabbi Akiva, a ben ger, who teaches it.

title.en: Yovel and the eighth level, with the Maharal

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that yovel is the Kodesh HaKodashim: the Torah was heard on the fiftieth day and the luchos came down on Yom Kippur, both glimpses of yovel. He brings the eight-stringed harp of Moshiach and reads the Maharal that the Kodesh HaKodashim, Chanukah, milah and the Torah are 'after seven', the eighth above nature.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai as yovel

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the dispute between Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai about working the land: Rashbi is the aspect of Shabbos, and even more, of yovel, the 'Shabbos of Shabbosos'. From the Gemara that 'hod' is the Beis HaMikdash he calls Rashbi the hod within hod, the Kodesh HaKodashim, and says Shavuos and Yom Kippur are both glimpses of yovel.

title.en: The aron that took no space

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the aron taking no space is not counted among the miracles of the Beis HaMikdash, and what purpose it served. He answers that the Kodesh HaKodashim, where creation began, is where heaven meets earth, and heaven is above measure, so it is its nature, not a miracle; likewise Rabbi Yehuda's fiftieth year counts for both cycles, and Moshe could add a day.

title.en: Why the children come to Hakhel

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the derashah of Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah on Hakhel: the men come to learn, the women to hear, and the children to give reward to those who bring them. He asks why Hashem would give a mitzvah whose only point is reward, with no purpose of its own.

title.en: David's fourth tefillah and fourth seudah

summary.en: The Mashgiach discusses David's prayer at chatzos and the Ramchal that it is not obligatory because David was lower than the Avos, and questions this from Midrash Tanchuma and the Gemara that Moshiach is greater than the Avos. He compares the three Shabbos meals to the Avos and melave malka to David, and explains why the end of Shabbos, bordering on the eighth, is its holiest moment.

title.en: Moshiach comes after shemitah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the Gemara that Moshiach comes at the end of shemitah: after seven comes eight, the world of Moshiach. He describes Moshiach's soul waiting in heaven, the tzaddik of each generation fit to receive it, and the doubt in heaven at every end of Shabbos and shemitah whether the next is the eighth or a new first, which also deepens Rabbi Yehuda's view of the fiftieth year.

title.en: Magen David and maftir

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar that David asked for a blessing like 'Magen Avraham' and was tested with Bas Sheva. He asks why 'Magen David' is said in the haftarah blessings but not in Shemoneh Esrei, and answers that David's greatness will only be understood in the eighth world of Moshiach, which maftir, the eighth aliyah, represents.

title.en: Rosh Hashanah and Hakhel in the eighth year

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the eighth year is still called 'the year of shemitah' and says the coming Rosh Hashanah is the 'shalosh seudos' of shemitah, tosefes upon tosefes. He reads the Rambam on Hakhel as a renewed Sinai and on the king as the heart of Israel, and explains that the king, Yerushalayim and Yom Kippur are the heart in soul, place and time, joining at Hakhel in the eighth year.

title.en: No waiting for Moshiach is wasted

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara against those who calculate the end, and its answer that one waits in order to receive reward, 'fortunate are all who wait for Him'. He explains that every Jew's hope joins the waiting of all generations and brings Moshiach closer, like money accumulating in an account.

title.en: The children's shirah and the hope of Hakhel

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that infants sang shirah at the Yam Suf and pointed, and says the future song will be greater. This answers his question: at Hakhel after shemitah the eighth world might be revealed, so parents bring their children in hope they will sing. When it did not come in hundreds of Hakhels, he answers as the Gemara does: the waiting is never wasted.

title.en: Accepting Hashem as King this Rosh Hashanah

summary.en: Returning to the mitzvah of appointing a king, the Mashgiach says the Rosh Hashanah after shemitah is an auspicious time for Moshiach, and one must prepare to accept Hashem as King instead of the desires that rule a person's life. He describes Moshiach's soul hovering like a bird looking for rest, leaves the opening questions unanswered for lack of time, and closes with blessings for a good year.

catalogTitle: דרשה בבית האסורים: English: Freedom in Prison אידיש: גודל תענוג השכינה מעבודה בעמקי הקליפות

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the light Hashem created on the first day is true freedom from the yetzer hara, and that accepting the kingship of Heaven even from the lowest place, as Yosef did when he left prison on Rosh Hashana, is what makes a person free.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens in English on the twenty-fifth of Elul, the first day of creation, when Hashem said 'Let there be light'. He explains that light means happiness, contentment and above all liberty, and that real liberty is being free to do the right thing; the greatest imprisonment is being bound to the yetzer hara, and the whole world is in that sense a big prison. Every person has an inner desire to serve his Creator, and the world awaits a Rosh Hashana when all mankind will hear Hashem's voice and be free to serve Him. After blessing his listeners, he continues in Yiddish with Tanya chapter 33: the purpose of creation is to bring holiness down to the lowest places, and serving Hashem from darkness, in galus and outside Eretz Yisrael, brings Him special joy. He ties this to Rosh Hashana as the day of malchus, to the chazan saying 'Hamelech' where he stands, and to Yosef leaving prison on Rosh Hashana, and closes with the shofar of freedom.

en: The light Hashem created with 'Let there be light' means happiness, contentment and above all liberty.
Real liberty is being free to do the right thing, and the greatest imprisonment is being bound by the yetzer hara and one's bad passions.
Every human being has an inner desire to serve Hashem, his Creator and Provider, and the world awaits a Rosh Hashana when all mankind will be free to serve Him.

Following Tanya chapter 33, the Mashgiach teaches that the main purpose of creation is to bring holiness down to the lowest places, and that this should give a Jew great joy wherever he finds himself.
Rosh Hashana is the time of accepting the kingship of Heaven, and malchus is brought down to the lowest place where a Jew stands.
A Jew in the lowest state, even in prison, must know that he has a mission from Hashem there and accept the kingship of Heaven there; whoever does so is a king and is free.

candidateTopics: Rosh Hashana and kingship of Heaven
avodah in galus and chutz la'aretz

title.en: Let there be light: light is liberty

summary.en: Speaking in English, the Mashgiach explains that the twenty-fifth of Elul is the day of creation and that Rosh Hashana falls on the sixth day, when Adam was created. He interprets the light of 'Let there be light' as happiness and liberty, and describes the greatest prison as being bound by the yetzer hara.

title.en: Awaiting a Rosh Hashana of freedom

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that on the first day Hashem meant freedom to serve Him, which every person inwardly desires, and that the world awaits a Rosh Hashana when all mankind will hear Hashem's voice and be free. He blesses his listeners with a kesivah vachasimah tovah and announces that he will continue in Yiddish.

title.en: Tanya 33: serving Hashem from the depths

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Tanya chapter 33, that the purpose of creation is to bring holiness into the lowest places and that subduing the sitra achra there brings Hashem joy. He applies this to serving Hashem in chutz la'aretz and in the last generations of galus, and to the Rosh Hashana theme of malchus and the cry 'from the depths'.

title.en: Yosef leaves prison on Rosh Hashana

summary.en: The Mashgiach suggests that this is why there is no aliyah l'regel on Rosh Hashana and why the chazan says 'Hamelech' where he stands. He explains that on Rosh Hashana Yosef left prison, the place of greatest lowliness, and that whoever accepts the kingship of Heaven there is a king and free; he closes with the shofar of freedom and blessings.

catalogTitle: The Rejuvenation of the World and of Mankind

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Rosh Chodesh Nissan, when man was created, is the time each year when the world is renewed, and that a Jew must renew himself with it, become a true Adam, and bind himself to Hashem through the emunah of Pesach.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the opinion that the world and man were created in Nissan, and describes Hashem's original plan for a perfect world without toil, illness or death. Adam HaRishon spoiled it with the sin of the Tree of Knowledge; Hashem began again with the Exodus and chose Klal Yisroel, who spoiled it with the Golden Calf; then He confined His holiness to the Mishkan, set up on Rosh Chodesh Nissan, which ended with the destruction of the Batei Mikdash. A fourth Rosh Chodesh Nissan is promised. Hashem allowed these failures to teach a Jew to start over after every failure. The Mashgiach then describes how the world comes back to life each Nissan and calls on each person to renew himself, to master the animal traits of his mazal, and to become an Adam. Pesach, the festival of Avraham Avinu, is the time of emunah: the bond of chasan and kallah with Hashem, eaten in the matzah and transmitted to children.

en: Hashem's original plan in creating the world in Nissan was a perfect world where man would live forever, without toil, worry or illness.
The plan was disappointed three times: Adam's sin, the Golden Calf after Klal Yisroel was chosen, and the destruction of the Mishkan and the Batei Mikdash; a fourth Rosh Chodesh Nissan is promised.
Hashem allowed these failures as a lesson: a Jew who fails must not tire but do teshuvah and start over again, every time.
In Nissan the whole creation is reborn and sings a new song, and a person who stays the same old self is left out of it.
Each person is born with a mazal resembling an animal, and he must master that trait and raise it for avodas Hashem.
Pesach, the festival of Avraham Avinu, is the time of emunah, when Klal Yisroel became Hashem's kallah; matzah is the food of emunah.
Eating chametz on Pesach cuts a person off, like eating from the Tree of Knowledge, while keeping Pesach binds him to Hashem like eating from the Tree of Life.

candidateTopics: matzah as the food of emunah
chametz and the Tree of Knowledge

title.en: Creation in Nissan and Hashem's original plan

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Na'aseh adam said on Rosh Chodesh Nissan, following Rabbi Yehoshua that the world was created in Nissan, and mentions Birkas HaChamah every 28 years. He then describes Hashem's intention: a perfect world without worry, illness or toil, where man lives forever and learns Torah.

title.en: Three disappointments and a fourth Nissan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Adam's sin spoiled the plan, stressing that Hashem's 'disappointment' and 'regret' are said in human terms. Hashem began anew at the Exodus with Klal Yisroel, which the Golden Calf spoiled, and then confined His holiness to the Mishkan set up on Rosh Chodesh Nissan, which ended in destruction; a fourth Rosh Chodesh Nissan with the third Beis HaMikdash is promised.

title.en: The lesson: start over again

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Hashem allowed three disappointments if He knew what would happen, and compares it to the Rosh Chodesh offering brought as an atonement for Hashem for diminishing the moon. He answers that it is a lesson: a Jew who fails in his avodah must not tire but do teshuvah and start over, again and again.

title.en: The world is reborn each Nissan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the newness of creation descends every Nissan, and paints the spring with the words of Shir HaShirim: the white shrouds of winter melt into green fields, flowers, birds and butterflies, and all of creation sings a new song to Hashem. He asks why man should stay the same old self while everything renews itself, and calls on each person to wake up and decide to be an Adam, not a beast.

title.en: Mastering the animal in man; renewal for Pesach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that each person is born under a mazal like the animals of the shevatim's brachos, and must be master over that trait and raise it for avodas Hashem. He adds that Nissan is a time of techiyas hameisim, and that everything on Pesach is new, from clothing to dishes, so a person should want to be new as well.

title.en: Avraham Avinu, emunah and matzah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that Pesach corresponds to Avraham Avinu, who baked matzos on Pesach, and that emunah is his inheritance to every Jew, hidden or revealed. Emunah is tied to Yetzias Mitzrayim, when Klal Yisroel became Hashem's kallah, with seven brachos at the Seder like sheva brachos; matzah is the food of emunah.

title.en: The bond of Pesach and the sin of chametz

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that emunah is transmitted to children through the Haggadah, and asks why only chametz on Pesach carries kares while transgressions on Shavuos and Sukkos do not. He answers that Pesach is the bond of chasan and kallah with Hashem, so chametz cuts one off, and brings from the sefarim that chametz and se'or equal the gematria of the Tree of Knowledge, while matzah is like eating from the Tree of Life.

title.en: Making a memorable Pesach

summary.en: The Mashgiach urges using the Yom Tov with yiras Shamayim and simchah: being scrupulous about Pesach food, saying the Haggadah and Hallel and eating matzah with joy, which gives emunah that lasts a lifetime. He mentions that the heavenly family comes to the Seder, brings Reb Chaim Meir of Vizhnitz on making a Pesach to remember, and thanks the yeshivah for the chance to speak.

catalogTitle: גודל כח סעודת מרעים: מקבלים השפעות גדולות מציל ממים הזידונים של גלות

oneLiner.en: At a melave malka held as a farewell seudah for a friend, the Mashgiach explains that Jews who eat together are bound into one group that receives a higher flow of life, and that this bond is a teivah that saves them from the waters of the present exile.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with melave malka as a seudah that escorts Shabbos and traces the farewell seudah to Shemini Atzeres. He tells a story from the Midrash, cited in teshuvos of the Divrei Chaim and the Chiddushei HaRim, of a couple who parted with a seudah and were then blessed with children. He then explains that Hashem sends greater hashpa'ah to a tzibbur, which becomes a new collective soul, and that eating together forms a zimun the same way; 'yachdav' means bound, not merely together. The Midrash reads the four 'vayigberu' of the Mabul as the four exiles, and the present Mabul of heresy is escaped through the teivah: Torah, tefillah and joining with friends. Finally he links the thirty letters of a line in a Sefer Torah to the chaburos of the korban Pesach, and applies all this to the seudah for their friend Menachem.

en: A tzibbur of ten becomes a new entity with a collective soul and can receive a hashpa'ah that even the greatest individual tzaddik cannot.
Eating is a receiving of life, and when several Jews eat together they form a zimun that receives a higher kind of life; the bond of zimun comes from the eating, not from the benching.
The Midrash teaches that the four times 'vayigberu' appears by the Mabul are the four exiles, so the Mabul is a living lesson for galus.
The way to be saved from today's Mabul is to run into the teivah: Torah, tefillah, Tehillim, and binding oneself with friends.
A line of thirty letters in a Sefer Torah corresponds to the three groups of ten in which the korban Pesach was slaughtered and eaten.

candidateTopics: the Mabul as an image of galus
the teivah as words of Torah and tefillah
friendship among those who fear Hashem

title.en: Melave malka and the farewell seudah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes melave malka as a small seudah escorting Shabbos as it leaves and traces the farewell seudah to Shemini Atzeres. He begins a teshuvah of the Divrei Chaim about a talmid chacham married ten years without children.

title.en: The couple who parted with a seudah

summary.en: The Mashgiach relates that the same question was sent to the Chiddushei HaRim, who ended with the Midrash of the childless couple who came to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai to divorce, parted with a seudah, and were blessed with children through his tefillah. He adds what a Sanzer descendant told him about the family's tradition.

title.en: Hashpa'ah to a tzibbur and through eating

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem sends each soul hashpa'ah through Torah, tefillah and eating, measured to what it can hold, and that ten Jews joined as a tzibbur become a new entity that receives more. Eating as a Jew should eat draws a holier kind of life, and several eating together form a zimun, which already brings the Shechinah with three.

title.en: Zimun comes from eating; 'yachdav' means bound

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chiddushei HaRim's reason why chassidim eat together after davening, and shows that the bond of zimun comes from eating together, not from benching together. From the passuk of zimun and the laws of shaatnez he proves that 'yachdav' means bound, not merely side by side.

title.en: Eating creates friendship; Ammon and Moav

summary.en: The Mashgiach says eating together creates lasting friendship and connection. Using the principle that not believing in techiyas hameisim is a sign rather than a punishment, he explains that Ammon and Moav's failure to bring bread and water showed they have no connection to the Jewish people.

title.en: The Mabul of today and the teivah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that the four times 'vayigberu' are the four exiles, so the Mabul repeats itself in galus, and today's Mabul is one of heresy and immorality. Citing the Ba'al Shem Tov that a teivah is a word of Torah and tefillah, he says a Jew must flee into it, as Noach did, and those who bind themselves to the tzaddikim will remain.

title.en: The four exiles: breadth, height and time

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes each exile: Bavel scattered the Jews in breadth, Madai brought Haman's decree, Yavan fought in height against the Shechinah, matching the fifteen amos the waters rose, and Edom contains them all and adds the dimension of time, an exile without a set end, matching the hundred and fifty days. The answer remains to flee into the teivah of Torah and tefillah.

title.en: Joining with friends as a teivah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says binding with friends is part of the teivah, bringing the Ruzhiner Rebbe's advice that Jews should gather and strengthen each other, and the command to Noach to take food into the teivah. He cites Malachi that in the final hester panim those who fear Hashem speak to one another, and tells of a talmid who complained that people come to sit with him, and was told that this itself is a great strength.

title.en: Thirty letters in a line and the korban Pesach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that a line in a Sefer Torah holds thirty letters, 'lemishpechoseichem' three times, and asks why it is learned from the korban Pesach and not from the earlier 'lemishpechoseihem' by Noach. He explains that souls come down in groups, that the korban Pesach was eaten in chaburos and slaughtered in three groups of thirty, and that leaving the teivah broke the group while the Pesach gathered it.

title.en: This seudah and the parting from Menachem

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies the ideas to the gathering: they are eating a melave malka bound to Shabbos and parting from their friend Menachem, and eating together binds them. He contrasts a passuk, which cannot be split, with a flexible line, and closes that everything written about the Mabul is a lesson for galus, noting the first passuk of Zichronos about Noach.

catalogTitle: Cell Phones: כינוס התעוררות בענין: חומר סכנת Cell Phones בלי הכשר

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach warns the young men of his shul against cellphones without a hechsher, from the leitzanus of text messages to the danger of immorality, and insists that the ruling of the Gedolim must be obeyed.

abstract.en: Speaking in the days of Selichos to the young men raised in his shul, the Mashgiach addresses a report that some have become absorbed in their cellphones. Text messages, he explains, remove the natural shame of face-to-face speech and breed a constant traffic of jokes and leitzanus, even during learning and davening. He brings a story of someone who left a meal rather than sit in a moshav leitzim, and the passuk that one cannot sit among scoffers and desire Hashem's Torah at once. New tools are new forms of the yetzer hara. Far worse, a phone with open features exposes a person to immorality. Using the Gemara in Bava Basra and the Rashbam, he explains that only someone who truly needs it for his livelihood may use one, and compares this to a heter given only for a pressing case. Ignoring the Gedolim's ban, he argues from zaken mamrei, Rabbeinu Yonah and the fall of American Jewry, cuts a person off from Hashem. He ends with practical guidance and a call to tefillah.

en: Text messages remove the shame of speaking face to face, so they become a channel for constant jokes and leitzanus.
A person cannot both sit among scoffers and truly desire Hashem's Torah; it is one or the other.
A cellphone with open features exposes its owner to the danger of immorality, which is far graver than leitzanus.
Only someone who must have such a phone for his livelihood may use it, and then he must guard himself; one who does not need it and takes it anyway is called a rasha.
Disobeying the Gedolei Yisrael who forbade such phones is akin to the sin of the zaken mamrei and cuts a person off from Hashem.
The Mashgiach calls on those without a business need to decide now to get rid of such a phone, and on everyone to daven daily for protection from the yetzer hara.

candidateTopics: new forms of the yetzer hara
Shlomo HaMelech and the king's wives

title.en: Text messages and the loss of shame

summary.en: The Mashgiach addresses the young men raised in his shul, says it is a time of seeking Hashem, and relates the report that some are absorbed all day in their cellphones. He explains that text messages remove the shame of face-to-face speech, breed leitzanus, and distract bochurim even during the shiur and davening.

title.en: Leaving a moshav leitzim

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a man who got up and left a family meal when a joke was made, because it was a moshav leitzim, and contrasts this with devoting a whole day to leitzanus by text. He tells the young men they are too choshuv to fall to such lowness.

title.en: Learning is Shabbos; new yetzer haras

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that during learning one treats the phone as on Shabbos, and that even a kosher phone does not belong in the beis medrash. One cannot both sit among scoffers and desire Hashem's Torah. He then speaks of new forms of the yetzer hara, such as movies and radio, that keep appearing.

title.en: A trembling world and the Mississippi drasha

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes a time when the world is in turmoil and dangers loom, and tells how the Chofetz Chaim gathered people for a drasha on teshuvah because the Mississippi had flooded in America. When Hashem shakes the world, he says, the message is for Jews; mocking such things by text is laughable, and the phone holds something worse than leitzanus.

title.en: The danger of zenus and the one who closes his eyes

summary.en: The Mashgiach warns that a phone with open features exposes a person to immorality, citing the passuk not to approach the door of her house. Rabbanim allowed it only for business; he brings the Gemara in Bava Basra and the Rashbam that one who walks a road of temptation without need is a rasha even if he shuts his eyes, while one with no other way becomes a ba'al bechirah who must guard himself.

title.en: A heter for one is treif for another

summary.en: The Gedolim forbade such phones and permitted them only for business. Through a mashal of two shailos on meat, one before Shabbos when the Mashgiach relies on the Rema's leniency for a pressing case and one on Sunday, the Mashgiach shows that what is permitted for one is forbidden for another. He adds that a single look can harm a person for life, and that zenus belongs to the sins of yehareg ve'al ya'avor.

title.en: Zaken mamrei and the yud of yarbeh

summary.en: The Mashgiach says disobeying the rabbanim is worse still: the Rambam calls the parsha of zaken mamrei the foundation of the Torah. He tells of Shlomo HaMelech, who relied on his own wisdom to take more wives, and asks why it was the yud of 'yarbeh' that complained; the yud stands for bitul, as Moshe added a yud to Yehoshua's name for his humility.

title.en: The Gedolim's ruling and Rabbeinu Yonah

summary.en: The Mashgiach stresses that the Gedolim of America and Eretz Yisroel forbade phones without a hechsher except for a business need, and one who disobeys is like a zaken mamrei. He brings the Gemara in Berachos and Rabbeinu Yonah, who explains the death penalty for disregarding the rabbanim, and the passuk of the judge 'in those days'; cleaving to talmidei chachamim is how one cleaves to Hashem.

title.en: Decide now; why American Jewry fell

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the gadol hador has the status of one's main rebbe, and calls on whoever has such a phone without a business need to decide now to give it up despite the cost. He explains that American Jews fell away because they did not listen to the rabbanim about kashrus, and that the word 'zadon' marks undermining the foundation of Yiddishkeit.

title.en: Who may use it, and how

summary.en: The Mashgiach praises the young men and says one must daven daily to be saved from the yetzer hara. He gives the example of a mechanech who must reach doctors and psychologists for his students: such a person may use it, but only during business hours, like chametz that is kosher all year and becomes treif. Doubts should go to a moreh hora'ah, and the principle of 'once permitted for a need' does not apply here.

title.en: No half-measures; tefillah and a brachah

summary.en: Blocking text service by calling the company is no real solution, since it can be restored with one call; the only solution is not to have it, and the main one is to ask Hashem for help. The tests of this generation come because it is being prepared for Moshiach, and the talk ends with blessings for the new year.

catalogTitle: חינוך: השבת אבידה של נשמות להקב"ה' מחנכים יחידים' יחזקאל - טענות הקב"ה על מלמדים שאינם נאמנים' אינו אובד תקוה על נשמה בישראל

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach speaks about bringing lost Jewish souls back to Hashem, Hashem's complaint against those who did not bring back the one who strayed, and the principle that among Jews nothing is ever beyond hope.

abstract.en: The shiur is a talk on chinuch: returning lost souls to Hashem as a kind of returning a lost object, the role of individual educators, Hashem's complaint in Yechezkel against teachers who are not faithful, and never giving up hope on a Jewish soul. The Mashgiach speaks of souls that are lost and of the one who strayed and was not brought back, in connection with people who went away from the tzaddikim. At the end he states that among Jews there is no such thing as saying that something cannot be, and that a Jew is never written off.

en: The Mashgiach speaks of Jewish souls that are lost to Hashem and need to be brought back.
He describes a complaint against those who did not bring back the one who strayed, when people went away from the tzaddikim.
He concludes that among Jews one can never say that something cannot be.

summary.en: The opening of the shiur.

title.en: The one who strayed was not brought back

summary.en: The Mashgiach mentions a soul that is lost and the coming of Moshiach, then speaks of a complaint that the one who strayed was not brought back, in connection with people who went away from the tzaddikim.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: No Jew is beyond hope

summary.en: The Mashgiach closes by saying that among Jews one can never say that something cannot be.

catalogTitle: מצה - A Food of אמונה and גאולה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that matzah is a food of emunah and of geulah, and that through the mitzvos of Pesach, from burning the chametz to eating the matzah and spilling the wine, the Jewish people wage their real war against their enemies.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying that this Pesach comes at a time of war against the Jewish people, and that Jews fight not with weapons but with Torah, tefillah, tzedakah and the mitzvos of Pesach. Pesach is the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu, whose trait is emunah, and the Zohar calls matzah the food of emunah. Bread contains all ten utterances of creation, while matzah, by gematria three times the filled-out Name of Hashem and three times geulah, holds the Names of the redemption itself. Our matzah is the same matzah the Jews ate in Mitzrayim, and on the Seder night the root of the soul is in Yerushalayim. The Mashgiach then speaks of Pesach as the beginning, of Nissan as a month of healing, of matzah as the key that opens the treasuries of blessing, of the four cups and the plagues, and of searching and burning the chametz, which this year falls on Shabbos, as the battle against Amalek and Yishmael.

en: The Mashgiach says the Jewish people wage war not with weapons but with Torah, tefillah, tzedakah and by keeping Pesach; the front is not far away but right here.
Pesach is the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu, whose trait is emunah, and matzah is called the food of emunah.
Lechem equals three times the Name Havaya (78), while matzah equals three times the filled-out Name (45), which is also the value of geulah, so matzah carries the Names of the redemption.
The matzah eaten today is the same matzah the Jews ate in Mitzrayim, and on the Seder night the root of the soul goes to Yerushalayim and eats it there.
Matzah is the key that opens the treasuries of blessing on the Seder night.
Searching and burning the chametz is the inner war against the yetzer hara and against the klipah of Amalek, Esav and Yishmael, and this year it is strengthened by the power of Shabbos.

candidateTopics: matzah as the food of emunah
gematria of matzah and the filled-out Name
four cups and the ten plagues
spiritual war against Amalek and Yishmael
Nissan as a month of healing

title.en: A Pesach of war

summary.en: The Mashgiach says this Pesach comes while the Jews are in a state of war, and explains that Jews fight with Torah, tefillah, tzedakah, Hallel and the Haggadah, not with weapons. He brings the Targum on Eichah about the shouts of the nations on the Har HaBayis, which are countered with tefillah.

title.en: Pesach, Avraham Avinu and emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the three Yamim Tovim correspond to the Avos and that Pesach belongs to Avraham Avinu, in whose life many events took place on Pesach. Avraham's trait is emunah, Pesach is the time to implant emunah in one's children and oneself, and matzah is a food that contains emunah.

title.en: Bread, matzah and the Names of geulah

summary.en: Like a scientist who sees what is inside a food, the Mashgiach explains that bread contains all ten utterances of creation and equals three times the Name Havaya. Matzah equals three times the filled-out Name, 45, which is also the value of geulah, so it holds the Names with which Hashem redeemed the Jews from Mitzrayim, and the Zohar calls it a food of emunah and of healing.

title.en: The same matzah as in Mitzrayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks what a piece of the matzah baked in Mitzrayim would be worth if an archaeologist found it, and answers that our matzah is that very matzah, since its holy Names are the same. He brings the Targum Yonasan that the clouds of glory carried the Jews to Yerushalayim to eat the Korban Pesach, and says that on the Seder night the root of the soul goes to Yerushalayim.

title.en: Believing is greater than seeing

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Galician tzaddik who boasted to the Kotzker that he sees the Ushpizin, and the Kotzker's answer that he believes they come, and believing is greater than seeing. So too, with emunah a Jew is in Yerushalayim at the Seder; matzah belongs to Avraham Avinu, and emunah, as the Rambam and Ramban discuss, is the foundation of all the mitzvos.

title.en: Pesach as the beginning, and kareis

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that in the order of levels Pesach is the smallest Yom Tov, which is why only half Hallel is said, but it is the beginning, like Avraham Avinu. He shows from the punishment of kareis for chametz, which has no parallel on Shavuos and Sukkos, and from the kareis for Pesach and milah, that Pesach binds a Jew to Hashem with emunah.

title.en: Nissan, healing and Yitzchak's blessing

summary.en: After a break, the Mashgiach brings the sefarim that Nissan is a month of healing between Adar and Iyar, whose initials spell the verse about Hashem as healer, and adds that matzah makes Nissan a month of emunah and healing in its own right. He brings the Targum Yonasan that Yitzchak blessed on the night of Pesach, when the treasuries of dew open, and Rashi that Yaakov's two kids were a Pesach and a Chagigah.

title.en: Matzah, the key to the treasuries

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the treasuries of dew open on the Seder night, which is why Tal is said the next morning, and brings the Chasam Sofer's reading of grain, wine and oil as halachah, aggadah and the secrets of Torah. All these blessings open with the matzah, which the Targum calls by a word meaning opening, and this is why some have the custom of marking the challah with a key on the Shabbos after Pesach.

title.en: The four cups and the plagues

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings two reasons for the four cups, the four mentions of a cup in the butler's dream and the four expressions of geulah, and explains that each plague was a blow to Mitzrayim and a healing for the Jews. Wine is spilled at the plagues because that is the bad part, and the Haggadah keeps multiplying the plagues because saying them activates them, which is the Seder's war against the klipah.

title.en: Searching and burning the chametz

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the ten pieces of chametz in the search correspond to the ten utterances and the ten powers of the soul, and that the inner meaning of the search is to remove the yetzer hara from the heart. He tells of Rabbi Yisrael of Vizhnitz asking a chassid to search his heart for chametz, and says that burning the chametz is a call for Hashem to burn the chametz of the world, the ten nations and above all Amalek.

title.en: Biur chametz on Shabbos against Esav and Yishmael

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that this year the chametz is nullified on Shabbos, and the power of Shabbos is great against Amalek, who works today through Yishmael. He shows that tashbisu equals Shema Yisrael and that Vaizasa, the last son of Haman, equals Moshiach ben David, brings the Gemara and the Bnei Yissaschar on the zarzir and the orev, tells a story of a simple Jew's tefillah that annulled a decree, and ends with a blessing to eat the Pesach offerings in Yerushalayim.

catalogTitle: חבורות: נחיצות לימוד ספרי חסידות שנתגלה להאיר בתוך חשכות זמננו של עיקבתא דמשיחא

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that in the darkness of ikvesa d'Meshicha the Torah of the Ba'al Shem Tov and his talmidim is the remedy Hashem sent for this era, and urges learning chassidic seforim, especially on Shabbos.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Gemara's demand for 'emunah yeseirah', an extra measure of faith, and explains that Amalek fights emunah differently in every generation, and hardest now, as Moshiach nears. He describes the signs of the times: a collapsing world economy and the danger surrounding Eretz Yisrael, which can only be met with miracles. Yaakov saved his greatest brachos for the time of 'kol goyim sevavuni', and Malachi's 'az nidberu yirei Hashem' shows that the remedy is to gather and strengthen one another. He then shows how Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov as the cure for haskalah, since every era receives what it needs, as Purim and the Megillah came with hester panim. Through R' Shlomo of Lutzk, the Degel and other sources he describes the Besht's greatness, and contrasts the loving voice of chassidic seforim with the rebuke of earlier mussar. He closes by urging Shabbos learning of chassidic seforim.

en: Every Jew has emunah, but the Gemara demands emunah yeseirah, and emunah has endless levels.
Amalek's war against emunah changes its tactics in every generation, and in the time before Moshiach he fights with all his strength because he sees his end coming.
The present situation of the world and of Eretz Yisrael is that of 'kol goyim sevavuni', the time for which Yaakov saved his greater brachos.
Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov and Chassidus as the remedy for the haskalah; where Chassidus spread, haskalah did not succeed.
Each era receives from Hashem what it needs, and the Torah of the Besht is the new necessity of this era, a foretaste of the Torah of Moshiach.
Chassidic seforim speak to the soul with love, as Malachi does, and this is how one must speak to the broken Jews of today.
The Mashgiach urges that besides mussar there should be a 'Shabbos-dik' learning, with groups learning chassidic seforim on Shabbos and Friday night.

candidateTopics: the Ba'al Shem Tov as remedy for haskalah

title.en: Emunah yeseirah and Amalek's war in every generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Gemara that one should hold on to emunah yeseirah, explains that faith has endless levels, and that Amalek fights it with new tactics in each generation, hardest now before Moshiach. He adds that avodas Hashem cannot be routine; yiras Hashem must be sought like hidden treasure, as earlier generations did.

title.en: Signs of the times and the danger to Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach says there is no doubt this is the time before Moshiach: the world economy is collapsing as the Gemara's signs describe, and Eretz Yisrael is surrounded by enemies arming themselves. He recalls the miracles of the Six Day War and says today's situation can only be met with miracles.

title.en: Yaakov's brachos saved for 'kol goyim sevavuni'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar that Yaakov received four brachos but used only the weakest against Esav, saving the other three for the time of 'kol goyim sevavuni', which he says is today. He then brings Daniel's prophecy of an 'eis tzarah' unlike any before.

title.en: The book of Malachi: 'az nidberu yirei Hashem'

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks which 'book' Daniel means by those 'written in the book', and brings the seforim that it is Malachi's 'sefer zikaron' for those who fear Hashem and speak to one another. Malachi, the last prophet, speaks to the last generation, and the talmidim of the Besht taught that the only counsel before Moshiach is to gather and strengthen each other.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov as the cure for haskalah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how haskalah, communism and Zionism tore away large parts of Klal Yisrael, and how Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov as the remedy, as He sent the end of prophecy against Greek philosophy. Where Chassidus spread, haskalah failed; today chassidic seforim are learned even in Litvish yeshivos, and each generation has its own changes.

title.en: Each era receives what it needs: the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem's program runs through eras, each with its own way of learning and paskening, and each sent what it needs. His example is the Gemara on the Megillah: before Purim it was not needed, but in the new era of hester panim one cannot be a Jew without it, and it brought a new kind of Torah of 'kiymu v'kiblu'.

title.en: The new era of the Besht and R' Shlomo of Lutzk's testimony

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a new era began with the Ba'al Shem Tov, a new way of avodah through love like that of Rashbi in the Zohar. He reads from R' Shlomo of Lutzk's introduction about the Maggid's greatness, his gilui Eliyahu, and what the Besht taught him: the speech of birds and trees, holy names and the angels of each month.

title.en: The Besht crossing the river with emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells from the Degel Machaneh Ephraim how the Besht crossed a dangerous river on his gartel, not through holy names but through simple emunah. He adds the Belzer tradition that every frum Jew even in Germany exists by the Besht's power, and that his talmidim called the Toldos Yaakov Yosef the Torah of Moshiach, a 'preview' of what will be learned then.

title.en: Speaking to the soul with love, as Malachi does

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how the Besht raised simple Jews to great levels, and brings the Ramchal on Moshe's 'shavisa shevi', a captive soul later identified with Rashbi, the Arizal and the Besht. He contrasts mussar seforim that teach through fear with the Besht's way of love: Yeshayahu opens with harsh rebuke, but Malachi, who speaks to the last generation, opens with 'ahavti eschem'.

title.en: Chassidic seforim on the greatness of Shabbos and mitzvos

summary.en: The Mashgiach says chassidic seforim speak of the praises of Jewish children, as in the Berditchever's zemiros, and of the greatness of Shabbos, Yom Tov, tefillah and mitzvos, which other seforim hardly address; the Pri Tzaddik speaks of Shabbos in almost every Torah. This warmed and comforted Jews worn out by a week of hard labor, and he notes that Shlomo HaMelech wrote mussar seforim too.

title.en: Shir HaShirim and a call for Shabbos learning

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Shir HaShirim, the song of love between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, the crowning work of Shlomo HaMelech, and says chassidic seforim draw from it. He gives his advice: alongside mussar, learn in a Shabbos-dik way that comforts Jews whose blackness is only external, and form groups to learn chassidic seforim on Shabbos and Friday night.

catalogTitle: ברכת החמה: יתפלל שרק ה' יהיה אור של בנ"י ויתגלה שהשפע שייך רק להם

oneLiner.en: On the day of Birchas HaChamah the Mashgiach explains that the sun's power of giving, which in exile seems to belong to Esav, truly belongs to Klal Yisroel, and that blessing the sun is a prayer that Hashem alone become Yisroel's light.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the teaching that the moon was given to Yisroel and the sun to the nations, and asks why Jews rejoice so much over a blessing on the sun. Citing the Toras Yeshaya on Rashi's first comment, he explains that Bereishis alludes to the sun and nature, and that every twenty-eight years Hashem wishes to hand the power of giving to Yisroel. From Rashi on Toldos he shows that Esav's greatness is borrowed from Yaakov. The blessing 'oseh maaseh bereishis' asks Hashem to return to the hidden light of creation, when no sun or moon was needed. He tells from the Bnei Yissaschar how the Chozeh of Lublin wrote down each month's events in the first twelve days of Nissan, notes the good sign that this year's blessing falls on the fourth of Nissan, the day of Tammuz, and calls for renewal, a cheshbon hanefesh and acceptance of Hashem's kingship.

en: The moon was given to Klal Yisroel and the sun to the nations, so some questioned why Jews rejoice so much over a blessing on the sun.
The sun is the giver and the moon the receiver; every twenty-eight years Hashem wishes to hand the sun's power of giving over to Klal Yisroel.
Esav's power is filled only from Yerushalayim's destruction, so in truth both the sun and the moon belong to Yaakov.
The blessing 'oseh maaseh bereishis' asks Hashem to bring back the hidden light of creation, when Hashem Himself, not the sun and moon, gives light.
The first twelve days of Nissan contain the whole year, and how a person conducts himself in them shapes his whole year.
This year the blessing falls on the fourth of Nissan, which corresponds to Tammuz, the month of the sun's dominion and of the churban, and the Mashgiach sees this as a good sign.
Every twenty-eight years a person should renew himself and return to the upright state in which Hashem created him.

candidateTopics: sun and moon as Esav and Yaakov
the power of giving belongs to Yisroel

title.en: Why rejoice over the sun?

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the moon was given to Yisroel and the sun to the nations, and asks why the blessing on the sun is a great simcha. He brings the Toras Yeshaya on Rashi's first comment: Bereishis alludes to the sun, the giver, and every twenty-eight years Hashem wishes to hand that power to Yisroel.

title.en: Esav's borrowed light and the hidden light

summary.en: From Rashi on Toldos the Mashgiach shows that Esav's power comes only from Yerushalayim's destruction, so sun and moon both belong to Yaakov. He explains 'oseh maaseh bereishis' as a request to return to the hidden light of creation, and reads Rashi on 'me'oros' to show that needing luminaries to give light is a lack.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's Nissan writings

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells, from the Bnei Yissaschar's own testimony, how the Chozeh of Lublin wrote down in the first twelve days of Nissan everything that would happen in each month of the year. He explains that these days contain the whole year, so a person's conduct in them shapes his year.

title.en: The fourth of Nissan against Tammuz

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls it a good sign that the blessing falls on the fourth of Nissan, corresponding to Tammuz, the month of the sun's strength and of the churban. Since a mitzvah Jews do with something puts strength into it, blessing the sun on that day is a sign that Esav's power will be taken away and the sun revealed as serving Yisroel.

title.en: Nissan renewal and the upright man

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Nissan as the month when everything blossoms and Klal Yisroel grows into a people ready for the Torah. He calls for a cheshbon hanefesh in the first twelve days, and says that every twenty-eight years a person should return to the upright state in which he was created and fit himself into the order of creation.

title.en: Accepting Hashem's kingship and closing brachos

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of renewing oneself and accepting the kingship of Hashem, calls the day a simcha shel mitzvah and a time of favor for prayer, and closes with prayers for a refuah and that, as they merited to bless the sun, they merit a new light on Tzion and to sanctify the moon in Yerushalayim.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: עבודת ימי תמוז ואב להביא משיח ע"י חיזוק בהתמדת התורה' הכנה לשבת' טובת עין' עבודת התפילה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches that the forty days from Tammuz to Tisha b'Av, the days of the meraglim's mission, hide a blessing and the spark of Moshiach, to be drawn out through hasmadah in Torah, preparation for Shabbos, a generous eye toward others' honor, and davening with kavanah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the meraglim, who went on their mission from the end of Tammuz until Tisha b'Av, and says these forty days are every year days of shlichus in which the meraglim's sin must be repaired. Through Balak, whose curse hid the root of Moshiach, he shows that the Three Weeks hide a blessing. The verse 'the days of the first grapes' hints that these days are under the power of evil, yet fruit can also ripen in them. Moshiach comes through Torah, so the bnei Torah must strengthen their hasmadah and use their time here to learn. He stresses the value of time, then preparation for Shabbos and for Shabbos davening. The meraglim's sin grew from jealousy over position, so the repair is to rejoice in another's honor, like Aharon. Kalev's tefillah leads to a discussion of davening aloud: its sources, its purpose of arousing kavanah, and its limits.

en: The forty days from Tammuz to Tisha b'Av are every year days of shlichus, in which one must repair what the meraglim spoiled.
Like Balak, whose curse hid the root of Moshiach, the Three Weeks look like days of curse but hold a blessing within.
Moshiach comes through Torah, so the bnei Torah, who carry the mesorah, must strengthen themselves in hasmadah.
Erev Shabbos is already a part of Shabbos, and one must prepare for Shabbos and for Shabbos davening rather than fall into it unprepared.
The meraglim's sin came from fear of losing their positions; its repair is to be content with another's honor.
Davening aloud is meant to arouse kavanah; it should be done with dignity and without strange noises or movements.

Balak and the root of Moshiach
ayin tovah and jealousy over honor

title.en: The meraglim's forty days and Balak's hidden blessing

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the meraglim's mission, from the end of Tammuz to Tisha b'Av, makes these forty days a time of shlichus every year. He then shows through Balak, from whom Ruth and David descended, that the curse of the Three Weeks hides the blessing of Moshiach.

title.en: The days of the first grapes

summary.en: The Mashgiach says one must not despair in these days but seek their blessing. He reads the verse 'the days of the first grapes' as a hint that these days are under the power of evil, which is why the meraglim fell, yet they are also days when fruit ripens and good can be brought out.

title.en: Moshiach comes through hasmadah in Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Or HaChaim that Moshiach will not come to those who neglect Torah, and explains that what is expected is not that all Jews learn, but that the bnei Torah not be idle. He reminds the listeners that they came here on a shlichus to bring Moshiach, and that the place and its clean air are suited for learning with hasmadah.

title.en: The blessing that remained, and the value of time

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that of Bilaam's blessings only the one on batei knesses and batei midrash remained. He then shows from the Rambam on kiddush hachodesh how central time is to Klal Yisrael, and says Torah and mitzvos in their proper time are worth far more.

title.en: Shabbos and erev Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Shabbos lets the neshama, torn from its source, reconnect, and that erev Shabbos is already a part of Shabbos, so it must not be wasted. He tells of a tzaddik who chose a match from a simple family because he saw how their home was ready for Shabbos by midday on Friday.

title.en: Preparing for Shabbos davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Chassidim davened later on Shabbos in order to prepare, not to sleep longer, and describes being ready, after mikveh and brachos, by the time of davening. He asks for moderation at the Friday-night meal so one can daven in the morning, and tells of Rabbi Aharon of Karlin, who said the true pleasure is the soul's pleasure.

title.en: The meraglim's sin: jealousy over position

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar that the meraglim, who were leaders, feared they would be replaced in Eretz Yisrael, and their personal interest made them speak badly of the land. He applies this to the honors in a group, such as aliyos, and says the repair is to know that such thoughts are worthless and to be content with another's honor.

title.en: The danger of the top, and Aharon's good eye

summary.en: The Mashgiach says it is best not to put oneself at the top, since what is on top is more easily disqualified, and that every small position brings great tests. He brings that Aharon merited to carry the choshen on his heart because he rejoiced in his heart over his younger brother Moshe's greatness.

title.en: Kalev's tefillah and the custom of davening aloud

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi that Kalev went alone to Chevron to pray at the graves of the Avos to be saved from the meraglim's counsel, and says these forty days call for special tefillah. Asked about loud davening, he traces the custom to the talmidim of the Ba'al Shem Tov, including Rabbi Aharon of Karlin, and to the Ba'al HaTanya's writings.

title.en: The halachic basis: a loud voice arouses kavanah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that in halacha all the talmidim of the Ba'al Shem Tov follow the Ba'al HaTanya. He brings the Gemara on answering amen yehei shmei rabbah 'with all one's strength', the two readings of it, and the Shulchan Aruch with the Acharonim, who explain that a loud voice arouses kavanah, as with the first verse of Krias Shema. He points to Ne'ilah, when everyone davens aloud.

title.en: Every Maariv is Kol Nidrei, but without strange noises

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of two Kotzker Chassidim and the Kotzker Rebbe's words that by them every supper is a seder and every Maariv is Kol Nidrei, so one need not wait for Ne'ilah to daven with kavanah. Following Rabbeinu Yonah he says the parts of praise are said aloud, but warns against squealing and strange movements that invite mockery.

title.en: Levels of davening, and the closing blessing

summary.en: The Mashgiach says those who daven better aloud should do so with fire but with order, and brings the Ruzhiner that the higher one is, the more the fire burns inside unseen. He describes levels from a loud voice to no visible motion at all, and closes with the wish that the curse of these days turn to blessing and the shlichus be fulfilled.

catalogTitle: A Time for the Renewal of אמונה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Nisan, the month of HaChodesh hazeh lachem, is the birth of Klal Yisrael as a nation of believers, and therefore the time for every Jew to renew himself and his emunah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Nisan as a beginning: of the Mishkan's avodah and of Klal Yisrael as a nation bound by Torah. He asks why Rashi calls HaChodesh hazeh lachem the first mitzvah when milah and gid hanasheh came earlier, and turns to the mitzvah of emunah. A Jew believes by inheritance, as maaminim bnei maaminim, like the instinct passed down in a beaver or spider; Avraham Avinu was a new species that completed creation. A Jew who denies is sick, his heart clogged by aveiros and forbidden food. There is also emunah through examining nature and history. Following the Rambam in Yesodei HaTorah ch. 8, the Torah rests on what millions saw at Sinai, not on one man's wonders. That answers Rashi: milah is kept only because Moshe told it, so HaChodesh was the first mitzvah, and its nature is renewal. Nisan, the head of all moadim, is the time to renew one's emunah, with matzah as its food.

en: Nisan is a beginning in several ways: the Mishkan's avodah began then, and Klal Yisrael became a nation, a people defined only by the Torah.
Jews believe in Hashem by inheritance, as maaminim bnei maaminim, an instinct passed down from Avraham Avinu.
A Jew who says he does not believe has a sick emunah: aveiros, and above all forbidden food, clog the heart that believes by instinct.
Following the Rambam, the Mashgiach explains that the Torah rests on the experience of millions at Har Sinai, not on the wonders of one man.
HaChodesh hazeh lachem is the first mitzvah because it was the first mitzvah Moshe Rabbeinu gave Klal Yisrael, and its essence is renewal.
Rosh Chodesh Nisan and Pesach are a time of teshuvah and renewal, when a Jew can become a new person and renew his emunah.
Matzah, which Chazal call food of emunah, strengthens the inborn emunah just as forbidden food weakens it.

candidateTopics: Har Sinai as the basis of belief

title.en: Nisan as a beginning and Rashi's question

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Nisan as a beginning: of Birkas HaChamah, of the avodah in the Mishkan, and of Klal Yisrael as a nation bound only by Torah. He asks why Rashi calls HaChodesh hazeh lachem the first mitzvah when milah and gid hanasheh came earlier, and introduces the mitzvah of emunah, which the Rambam counts and the Ramban calls the foundation of all mitzvos.

title.en: Emunah by inheritance from Avraham

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how one can be commanded to believe and why Anochi Hashem is a statement rather than a command. He answers that Jews are maaminim bnei maaminim who believe by instinct, like a beaver building a dam or a spider spinning a web, and that Avraham Avinu was a new species whose arrival completed creation.

title.en: When emunah becomes sick

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares a Jew who denies Hashem to a body whose natural hunger was spoiled by eating sawdust: his emunah is not missing but sick. Aveiros, and especially forbidden food, clog the heart, so one must be very careful with kashrus and seek a healer of the soul.

title.en: Emunah through examining the world

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes a second kind of emunah, reached by examining nature, the human body and history. A wristwatch cannot assemble itself, so the claim that the universe came by itself is an excuse not to keep the Torah; he brings the Ramban that daily life is full of hidden miracles.

title.en: The mesorah of millions at Sinai

summary.en: Since emunah is a mitzvah it has halachos, and the Rambam teaches that it rests on mesorah. Other faiths followed one charismatic individual; the Torah was heard by millions at Har Sinai, and such a public event cannot be faked, just as no one can deny George Washington or Julius Caesar.

title.en: The Rambam: belief in Moshe from Sinai, not wonders

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the other faiths also accept that the Torah was given at Sinai but watered it down, claiming Hashem changed His mind. He brings the Rambam in Yesodei HaTorah ch. 8 that Jews did not believe Moshe because of his wonders, which leave a doubt of magic, but because they themselves saw Hashem speak to him at Sinai.

title.en: Answering Rashi: the first mitzvah through Moshe

summary.en: Returning to Rashi, the Mashgiach answers that milah is kept not because Avraham passed it down but because Moshe Rabbeinu told it, so HaChodesh hazeh lachem was the first mitzvah. Its very character is renewal: as a new moon appears in a dark sky, a new nation came out of the darkness of Mitzrayim.

title.en: Renew yourself: the fountain of youth

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that the mitzvah of HaChodesh tells each Jew to renew himself, citing Rabbeinu Yonah that a baal teshuvah is a new person and the words of Kiddush Levanah. Every Rosh Chodesh, and more so Rosh Chodesh Nisan, is a time of teshuvah; the fountain of youth the nations searched for is HaChodesh hazeh lachem, a mikveh in which to take new resolutions.

title.en: Pesach, head of the moadim, and nature's renewal

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Pesach is the head of all the moadim and the only one carrying kares, since its essence is a new bond with Hashem, the opposite of being cut off. Because the nation was renewed in Nisan, all of nature renews itself then, and a person should not be the exception.

title.en: Avraham's miracles and matzah, food of emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Avraham Avinu's miracles all happened on Pesach, since he was the first Jew. He concludes that one renews one's emunah through matzah, which Chazal call food of emunah, and that is why kosher matzah matters so much, and closes with a brachah for a Pesach of renewed emunah.

catalogTitle: נביא: דרוש בענין: אליהו הנביא בהר הכרמל - נשמה של לע"ל שיתקן כל יהודי

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains Eliyahu HaNavi's offering on Har HaCarmel as the descent of a soul from the world of tikkun to lift up Jews who are outside the camp, so that in the end Yerushalayim will reach as far as Damascus and every Jew, even a Gechazi, will reach his tikkun.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Eliyahu's offering on Har HaCarmel at a time when sacrifices outside the Beis HaMikdash were forbidden, and with Rabbi Yochanan's statement that Eliyahu will expound the passage of neveilah and treifah. He lays down that a tzaddik must sometimes descend to lift the fallen, and applies it to Gechazi, whom the Mishnah excludes from the World to Come but the dorshei reshumos include. Through Pri Tzaddik he shows that a metzora cannot enter Yerushalayim, the camp of Israel, while Damascus is the seat of Naaman's lasting tzaraas. Eliyahu, a soul above sin, already stood in the future Yerushalayim, which will spread to Damascus, so the outcasts will be found inside it. He adds gematrios, the spelling Darmesek in Divrei HaYamim, and the role of Eliyahu in answering every kushya. He closes with Elul as Eliyahu's month, the low state of our generation and the great worth of its small avodah.

en: A tzaddik sometimes has to come down from his level, even to a trace of the sin itself, in order to lift up those who have fallen.
By offering outside on Har HaCarmel, Eliyahu reached the Jews who stood outside the camp of Israel and brought them to cry out that Hashem is G-d.
When Moshiach comes Yerushalayim will spread as far as Damascus, so that even those who cannot enter Yerushalayim, like Gechazi, will find themselves inside it.
Eliyahu will answer every kushya, because each difficulty in the Torah reflects a kushya on some Jew, and answering it brings that Jew back.
Elul is Eliyahu's month, the month of Gad, when the building of Yerushalayim begins and a time of tikkun for every soul.
Our generation has been thrown down into 'Damascus', and its small avodah is more precious to Hashem than the great avodah of earlier generations.
