title.en: Eliyahu's offering outside on Har HaCarmel

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Eliyahu offering a korban on Har HaCarmel when sacrifices outside the Beis HaMikdash were forbidden, and asks why he then needed atonement and exile. He brings the passuk in Yechezkel that the kohanim may not eat neveilah and treifah, and Rabbi Yochanan's statement that Eliyahu will expound it.

title.en: A tzaddik descends to lift the fallen

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why specifically Eliyahu will expound this passage, recalling that 'teiku' means Eliyahu will answer all questions. He lays down the principle that a tzaddik must sometimes fall from his level, with the parable of one on a roof who must climb down to lift something from the ground.

title.en: Moshe, Gechazi and the camp of Israel

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies the principle to Moshe Rabbeinu and the egel, then turns to Gechazi, whom the Mishnah excludes from the World to Come, and to the Gemara that Elisha went to Damascus to bring him back. Through the Pri Tzaddik he explains that Gechazi's lasting tzaraas keeps him out of Yerushalayim, the camp of Israel, and so out of the World to Come.

title.en: Eliyahu lifts those outside the camp

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the Mishnah with the dorshei reshumos, who give Gechazi a share in the World to Come, and speaks of Jews who are driven outside the camp. Comparing them to a korban slaughtered outside the azarah, he explains that Eliyahu offered outside to lift such souls, and therefore needed atonement and went into exile toward Damascus.

title.en: Eliyahu, a soul above sin and time

summary.en: The Mashgiach offers a second approach: Eliyahu never transgressed, since his soul has no connection to sin and belongs to the world of tikkun. He brings the Gemara where Eliyahu answered Rabbah bar Avuha in a cemetery of goyim, the Targum Yonasan that Pinchas is Eliyahu, and the teaching that in the days of Moshiach the halachah will follow Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the soul of Shabbos.

title.en: Yerushalayim and Damascus as opposites

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that in the future Yerushalayim will reach Damascus, so Har HaCarmel will be within Yerushalayim and from Eliyahu's standpoint his offering was not outside. He explains that Yerushalayim and Damascus are opposites: Damascus is the seat of Naaman's lasting tzaraas, which drew Gechazi there, and tzaraas comes from lashon hara and machlokes.

title.en: When Yerushalayim reaches Damascus

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that when Yerushalayim spreads to Damascus the outcasts will find themselves inside it. He brings the Yalkut that the Beis HaMikdash will stand on Har HaCarmel among other mountains, gematrios linking Eretz HaCarmel to Yerushalayim and Boneh Yerushalayim Hashem to Aram Damesek, and explains Eliyahu's flight to Damascus and his anointing of Chazael as showing his mastery over Damascus.

title.en: Darmesek in Divrei HaYamim

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Divrei HaYamim always spells Damascus 'Darmesek' with a reish. He explains that the twenty-four books of Tanach parallel the twenty-four adornments of the bride and the combinations of Hashem's Name of malchus, that Divrei HaYamim is the last book which completes malchus and leans toward the world of tikkun, and that Darmesek equals machaneh Yisrael; with Eliyahu's power Elisha went there to repair Gechazi.

title.en: Eliyahu, Elisha and Gechazi; answering every kushya

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chiddushei HaRim that the highest gilui Eliyahu is when Eliyahu comes with Elisha and Gechazi runs after them. He explains that every Jew is a letter in the Torah, so a kushya in the Torah reflects a kushya on some Jew, and toiling to answer it brings that Jew to teshuvah; this is Eliyahu's task of 'teiku' and of turning the hearts of fathers to sons.

title.en: Why only Eliyahu can explain neveilah and treifah

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to the opening question: the passuk of neveilah and treifah remains difficult because souls rooted in it belong to the klipos and have no tikkun until the future, so only Eliyahu can expound it. He adds that Eliyahu is the angel of the bris, tied to the circumcision of the heart hinted in the word Elul.

title.en: Elul, the month of Gad and of Eliyahu

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Eliyahu comes from the tribe of Gad and Elul is Gad's month, when the building of Yerushalayim and of malchus begins, from Tisha B'Av through the reading of Sefer Devarim. He tells how a grandson of Rabbi Yitzchak of Skver ran to see Eliyahu and instead came to a right thought about parnassah, and says that whoever spends Elul properly receives Eliyahu by Erev Rosh Hashanah.

title.en: Our generation thrown into Damascus

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the footsteps of Moshiach as the lowest generation, with trials of a kind earlier generations never faced, and says we have been thrown into Damascus. He explains that we must repair what the great souls could not reach, and that Hashem watches over us like a babysitter, present even in the lowest depths.

title.en: The worth of small avodah

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that the small avodah of our generation is more precious than the great avodah of earlier ones: a Jew who does not look in the street gives up his will, which is mesiras nefesh. He brings the Maggid of Mezritch's parable of the king who delights in a talking bird, and the Sidduro shel Shabbos parable of the servant who brought a simple pearl from the depths of the sea, which the king placed at the head of his crown.

title.en: Every Gechazi will reach his tikkun

summary.en: The Mashgiach says we are all Gechazis in the time of Damascus, but Elul, the time of Eliyahu and of good thoughts, is coming, when Jews learn Tikkunei Zohar. He concludes that when Moshiach comes Eliyahu will come with Elisha and Gechazi, prays on the Shabbos of blessing the month of Elul that Yerushalayim reach our Damascus, and blesses that each one work on his own Gechazi.

catalogTitle: יארצייט: יארצייט של ר' שרגא פייוול מענדלאוויץ זצ”ל (ג' אלול)

oneLiner.en: On the yahrtzeit of Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, the Mashgiach describes him as an eved Hashem whose whole life was a Shabbos niggun of shleimus and harmony, a song that still sings in the yeshiva.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the end of the Torah: Moshe is called both 'ish ha'Elokim' and 'eved Hashem', and Yehoshua, who wrote the last pesukim, could describe him only from his own level, as eved Hashem. Like a blade of grass that also benefits from the sun, the Mashgiach will describe Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz as an eved Hashem: a builder of Torah in America who sat in the last bench and refused titles. His deepest teacher was his own neshamah, a neshamah of Shabbos, which is shleimus, and of shirah, which is harmony, like seven notes making one melody. The Mashgiach brings the 'seventh' in creation, Eretz Yisrael as a land of song, and stories of a torn leaf whose song was interrupted. Every life is a niggun; his was a Shabbos niggun, seen in his love of creation's beauty, the flowers he planted, the harmony he made between groups, the best talmidim he gave away, and his kabbalos. His niggun still sings.

en: Yehoshua could describe Moshe only as 'eved Hashem', from his own level; likewise the Mashgiach describes Reb Shraga Feivel as an eved Hashem.
Reb Shraga Feivel built Torah in America yet wanted no honor or title, preferring to remain a plain Jew.
His main teacher was his own neshamah, a neshamah of Shabbos and of shirah: Shabbos is shleimus, and shirah is harmony.
Every part of creation sings shirah to Hashem, and every person's life is a niggun; his life was one long Shabbos niggun.
As an eved Hashem he sent his best talmidim to build other yeshivos, and his niggun still sings in the yeshiva.

candidateTopics: chinuch of each bochur according to his way

title.en: Moshe: ish ha'Elokim and eved Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the last parsha of the Torah, where Moshe is called 'ish ha'Elokim', and explains that Yehoshua, who wrote the last pesukim, could describe him only as 'eved Hashem'. Comparing himself to a blade of grass that also benefits from the sun, he says he too will try to describe Reb Shraga Feivel.

title.en: A builder of Torah who sat in the last bench

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Reb Shraga Feivel as an eved Hashem: he planted Torah in America, yet sought no honor, sat in the last bench at the dedication of the new building he had organized, and taught his talmidim Tanya and Shaarei Teshuvah. He did not take a title and preferred to remain a plain Jew.

title.en: A neshamah of Shabbos and of shirah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Reb Shraga Feivel's main rebbe was his own neshamah, a Shabbos neshamah: on Erev Shabbos he became a different person. Shabbos is shleimus, and shirah is harmony, like seven notes; he brings the 'seventh' in creation and Eretz Yisrael as a land of song, and concludes that Reb Shraga Feivel was not limited to one area but was a neshamah of shleimus.

title.en: The leaf that sings

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how in camp Reb Shraga Feivel stopped a talmid who tore off a leaf, since he had interrupted its shirah, and how in Monsey he saw one leaf moving among still ones as the chazan. He adds that Reb Shraga Feivel would repeat that every person's life is a niggun sung to Hashem.

title.en: Beauty of creation and harmony between groups

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Reb Shraga Feivel taught bochurim to develop a sense for the beauty of creation in order to thank Hashem, bringing David Hamelech and the Rambam. In Monsey he planted flowers among the first things, and in the yeshiva he made a harmony between Hungarian Jews, Litvish roshei yeshiva and chassidus.

title.en: Giving away his best talmidim

summary.en: The Mashgiach relates that Reb Shraga Feivel sent his best talmidim to found other yeshivos, and he tells the bochurim to remember, when they are in business, what it means to give one's best people to a competitor. He did this because he was an eved Hashem.

title.en: A path for each bochur; the niggun still sings

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Reb Shraga Feivel had no single method but a separate path for each bochur, and tells of kabbalos found after his passing: to find a new idea every day to improve the yeshiva and to love every bochur. He concludes that his spirit remains in the yeshiva and his niggun is still sung.

catalogTitle: הכנסת כלה: א מצוה באזונדער מסוגל אויף ביאת המשיח (ביאור ענין יחוד קוב"ה ושכינתיה' עניניא דיומא - ערד ציטערניש בהייטי)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that hachnasas kallah stands out among the mitzvos as a source of rescue and of bringing the geulah, because the aim of every mitzvah is the union of Hashem, the Chassan, with Klal Yisrael, the Kallah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the teaching of Rabbi Dovid of Lelov that hachnasas kallah, placed in the list of birchos hashachar between visiting the sick and what comes after, saves a person from what follows it, and says one should give for it knowing it is a great rescue. He turns to the unsettled times and the earthquake in Haiti, citing the passuk in Tehillim that Hashem looks at the earth and it trembles, and tells how the Chofetz Chaim gathered his town in Radin to speak about a flood on the Mississippi. He explains the reason from Rashi in Parshas Va'eira: Hashem brings punishment on the nations so that the Jews take mussar, and he calls for strengthening in every area. Then he explains 'leshem yichud': every mitzvah aims at uniting the Chassan and the Kallah, so hachnasas kallah itself arouses Heaven most, and he closes with a brachah for the geulah.

en: Following Rabbi Dovid of Lelov, hachnasas kallah stands between visiting the sick and what follows it because it rescues a person from what comes after.
A disaster among the nations, like the earthquake in Haiti, is meant for the Jews, as Rashi says that Hashem punishes the nations so that the Jews will fear and take mussar.
The Mashgiach says Jews must take this to heart and strengthen themselves in every area, including the chinuch of children and tznius in dress.
Every mitzvah is said 'leshem yichud', for the union of Hashem, the Chassan of Shir Hashirim, with Klal Yisrael, His Kallah, who are now apart in galus.
Since the aim of every mitzvah is a kind of hachnasas kallah, the actual mitzvah of hachnasas kallah arouses Heaven more than any other.

candidateTopics: Hashem and Klal Yisrael as chassan and kallah

title.en: Hachnasas kallah rescues from what follows

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the great nachas in Heaven from helping Jews marry off their children, and brings Rabbi Dovid of Lelov's teaching that hachnasas kallah, placed in birchos hashachar between visiting the sick and what follows, saves from what comes after. He says that had he known this, he would have given far more, and that one should give knowing it is a great rescue from harsh decrees.

title.en: The Haiti earthquake and the Chofetz Chaim

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the unsettled times and the earthquake in Haiti, brings the passuk in Tehillim that Hashem looks at the earth and it trembles, and asks what it has to do with Jews. He tells how the Chofetz Chaim gathered the whole town of Radin for a drasha about a flood on the Mississippi, so that people should not ignore it.

title.en: Rashi in Va'eira: punishment of nations is for the Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the earthquake came in the week of Parshas Va'eira, where Rashi brings the passuk in Tzefaniah that Hashem destroys nations so that the Jews will fear and take mussar. He explains that the disaster is a message to Jews everywhere, that great plans for geulah are being prepared in Heaven, and that Jews must strengthen themselves in every area.

title.en: Leshem yichud: the Chassan and the Kallah

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why hachnasas kallah, of all mitzvos, is the one placed as the interruption. He explains 'leshem yichud' said before every mitzvah: Hashem and Klal Yisrael are Chassan and Kallah as in Shir Hashirim, separated in galus, and every mitzvah aims at their union in the geulah.

title.en: Collectors during davening; the women's resolution

summary.en: The Mashgiach addresses complaints about collectors for hachnasas kallah going around during davening and says he thanks such a person, because he reminds him that his davening is meant to be hachnasas kallah. He praises the women's resolution to work for hachnasas kallah, the mitzvah that arouses Heaven most, and closes with a brachah for the geulah.

catalogTitle: The Great קדושה of the מצה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Pesach, the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu, is the foundation of emunah, and that matzah, the 'food of emunah', carries within it the full holiness of Hashem's Name with which the Jews left Mitzrayim.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Birkas haChamah, which will fall on Erev Pesach the following year, and with the dispute whether the world was created in Tishrei or in Nisan: Tishrei is din and thought, Nisan is chesed and deed, the month in which everything is renewed. He then matches the three Regalim to the Avos and shows that Pesach belongs to Avraham, the beginning of the Jewish people and of emunah; only Pesach carries kareis, because it is the bond with Hashem. The Zohar calls matzah the food of emunah, and eating it makes emunah part of a Jew. Through the foods of animals and of man he shows that bread holds all of creation, that lechem is three times Hashem's Name and matzah three times its filled-out form. He closes by urging care with matzah and chametz, which the Zohar calls the yetzer hara.

en: Pesach is the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu, the beginning of the Jewish people; Shavuos and Sukkos are greater, but the beginning is the main thing.
Only Pesach carries the penalty of kareis, because Pesach is what binds a Jew to the Ribono shel Olam.
Emunah, the foundation of all mitzvos, comes from Avraham, and therefore the mitzvah of telling the children, the transmission of emunah, is on Pesach.
Matzah is the food of emunah; it is a mitzvah that is eaten and absorbed, so that emunah becomes part of a Jew.
Lechem equals three times Hashem's Name, while matzah equals three times its filled-out form, so matzah holds the Name in its fullness.
Chametz is the yetzer hara, which explains the great strictness about it and the search to remove it before Pesach.

kareis and the bond with Hashem

title.en: Birkas haChamah on Erev Pesach

summary.en: The Mashgiach mentions the dispute whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nisan, and notes that next year Birkas haChamah, said once in 28 years, falls on Erev Pesach, when the sun returns to its place at creation. He adds that this coincidence happened only a few times in history, among them the year of Yetzias Mitzrayim.

title.en: Tishrei and Nisan: din and chesed

summary.en: The Mashgiach ties Rabbi Eliezer's Tishrei to Beis Shammai's midas hadin and Rabbi Yehoshua's Nisan to Beis Hillel's chesed, bringing Rashi that creation was first planned with din and then joined with chesed. He then describes Nisan as the month of renewal: budding trees, new songs, the tradition that techiyas hameisim will be on Pesach, and its pleasant weather.

title.en: Pesach, the Yom Tov of Avraham Avinu

summary.en: The Mashgiach matches Pesach, Shavuos and Sukkos to Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, lists the events of Avraham's life that happened on Pesach, and explains that Pesach, though not the highest Yom Tov, is the beginning and therefore the main thing. Only Pesach carries kareis, since it is the bond with Hashem, and an areil cannot bring the korban Pesach.

title.en: Matzah, the food of emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Avraham is yesod and emunah is the yesod of all mitzvos, so the mitzvah of telling the children is on Pesach, and the Zohar calls matzah the food of emunah. He raises the question how one can say 'Ha lachma anya' over a different matzah, and explains that matzah is a mitzvah one ingests, so emunah becomes part of a Jew.

title.en: Lechem, matzah and Hashem's Name

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that each animal eats food that matches its middah, while man, who contains all of creation, eats bread, which contains all ten. Lechem is three times Hashem's Name and matzah three times its filled-out form, so matzah carries the holiness with which the Jews left Mitzrayim, and therefore one can truly say 'Ha lachma anya'.

title.en: Care with matzah; chametz and the yetzer hara

summary.en: The Mashgiach urges care with matzah, the bond with Hashem, brings Targum Yonasan that the Jews were carried to Yerushalayim to eat the korban Pesach, discusses machine and hand matzah, and asks for matzah baked with yiras Shamayim at least for the Seder. He then brings the Radbaz that chametz is the yetzer hara, tells of a tzaddik searching himself with a candle, and calls on the listeners to use the special year when Erev Pesach falls on Shabbos.
